Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field that can manipulate electromagnetic waves effectively  
by integrating multiple layers within an ultra-thin depth, nevertheless,  
investigating this complex system poses significant challenges due to its sensitive  
requirements and interconnected variables. To overcome these obstacles, we have  
developed a cutting-edge computational framework that integrates full-wave  
simulations and rational approximation to investigate the comprehensive response  
of metasurfaces across a wide frequency spectrum. This approach enables us to assess  
their theoretical capabilities in filtering, wave shunting, and wave manipulation,  
with particular emphasis on practical considerations such as power, speed, and  
efficiency. To illustrate the effectiveness of this method, we have examined a  
notch filter based on magnetic ensembles, exploring its performance through  
simulations and experimental evidence. Furthermore, we have explored how this  
approach can be utilized to design bespoke metasurfaces tailored to specific  
applications.

The primary objective of this research is to establish the feasibility of local orbital linearization for totally integrable vector fields with a non-degenerate singular point in R^n. Additionally, we will determine sufficient conditions for local orbital linearization of a singular point. These conditions involve a thorough analysis of the sensitivity of the integration curves within a specific family to slight modifications in the vector field. Both theoretical aspects and practical applications of this sensitivity are explored through examples of vector field families.

This study proposes a novel approach to model complex molecular properties. In cases with multiple electrons, complete configuration interaction methods are the gold standard, yet their practical application is limited to small systems. We introduce an advanced learning algorithm that can efficiently interpolate electron correlation within CI-complete one-electron manifolds. Trained on a set of ionized hydrogen atoms, this model exhibits precise accuracy across a range of systems. Furthermore, the method can be extended to apply to arbitrary molecules and atoms.

We discovered a massive galaxy group, named EBiDPM22-23, using the SkyNet X-ray catalog from the Swift-NESWATCH survey, which is particularly faint and distant, located far beyond the Milky Way's virial radius. This massive curve in the sky is composed of multiple gas halos that together form an enormous structure, occupying a vast volume of space and spanning an impressive 1.4 gigaparsecs³. Its total mass is estimated to be enormous, which makes it one of the most massive known structures in the universe.

The utilization of photometric data from well-established, photometry-based exoplanet transit timing variations (PBTTV) has significant potential in novel applications, particularly in the area of aerosol measurement. As more than 400,000 stars within the Milky Way are being continuously monitored as part of the ZTRANSIT project, they present an opportunity to leverage high precision, sub-mmmSss photometry to overcome the limitations of current satellite systems, which are limited in scope, to track changes in the Earth's atmosphere with greater accuracy. Although ground-based data is impacted by atmospheric conditions, the high precision photometry employed bypasses a certain type of atmospheric distortion, thereby enhancing its sensitivity to aerosol changes, which typically result in smaller stellar brightness fluctuations. Through analysis and simulation, we demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, which is limited primarily by our ability to calibrate the observations, as shown by a detection of varying stellar brightness caused by night-time cloud formations. Given the prevalence of clouds on Earth, which vary significantly based on the time of year, we infer that our method could potentially contribute to the monitoring of Earth's atmosphere, which is often compromised by rising temperatures, as well as the release of methane gas, by providing a precise, continuous, photometry-based system, which is unaffected by limited satellite coverage.

This paper introduces DeepHMap++, a novel end-to-end neural network approach for object pose estimation in six degrees of freedom. Building on the DeepHMap framework, our method enhances clustering and correspondence learning stages to improve pose prediction accuracy. In the first stage, we use a clustering projection network to group high-dimensional hidden map vectors into fewer 2D pixels, thereby reducing information loss and preventing overfitting. The second stage involves a correspondence learning network that maps the revised hidden map back to the target image, allowing for more effective synchronization between CLIP and TCP stages. Our method retains the benefits of DeepHMap while outperforming its original version, as demonstrated through rigorous experiments on the real-world datasets.

Nonlocal theories have gained significant attention in recent years due to their ability to nonlocally model phenomena occurring over extended distances, which cannot be modeled by classical partial differential equations. This property makes them particularly useful for describing materials that exhibit degradation, damage, and the propagation of cracks, as well as the mixing and movement of fluids through porous media. This review introduces a novel class of nonlocal models known as bond-oriented theories, exploring their mathematical foundations, as well as their similarities and differences with alternative nonlocal models. It also introduces recent research utilizing these bond-oriented models, including their application to the development of cracks in brittle materials and the creation of technical textures in fluid dynamics. This exploration demonstrates the potential of these models and highlights the need for more in-depth studies to validate their predictions.

Graphical Lasso is a widely used algorithm for efficiently estimating large sparse conditional random fields and Markov random networks. While the Generalized Graphical Lasso extends this method to more complex models, there is currently no corresponding Python library available. A new open-source Python library called GGLasso has been developed to fill this gap, utilizing the Sequential Minimal Graphical Lasso algorithm to solve the Generalized Graphical Lasso problem.

Numerous simulation techniques are utilized in computational chemistry and material science to calculate the conformational energy of molecules and materials, as well as their structural formations, from most stable configurations to chaotic states. These simulations can be prone to trapping systems in local minima, compromising their accuracy, especially when dealing with complex configurations characterized by numerous degrees of freedom. A new study was conducted to assess the reliability of six molecular simulation methods by comparing their ability to explore configurational spaces, measured through mutual information between molecular configurations and internal energies. Four methods, including simulated annealing, simulated tempering, parallel tempering, and Langevin dynamics, were evaluated, along with a modified version of LD utilizing an expanding harmonic well. Analysis was performed on benzenecarboxylic acid trimers, hair polymers, and a two-patch colloidal wall model. Results showed that a modified LD method consistently outperformed other methods, showcasing remarkable efficiency in exploring the energy landscape of molecules toward the ground state, as well as the structural formations of materials. These findings indicate that a carefully selected simulation method can effectively overcome shortcomings associated with systems exhibiting multiple stable configurations, enhancing the accuracy of molecular and material structure simulations.

This research builds a new computational model for simulating the interaction between two merging black holes and the surrounding cloud of objects orbiting them. The simulation takes into account the dynamics of general relativity for the black holes, a previously developed method for modeling the movement of discrete objects in a gravitational field, and a novel approach combining these elements using high-performance computing. The underlying method for tracking the movement of discrete objects was initially introduced by Porter and Gualdroni in 2017, and our enhancement significantly improves the efficiency of the computation through use of the EXA烃 project's Anton blue supercomputer, allowing for a more detailed and accurate simulation over an extended period. A key focus area in the research was how the merging black holes disturb the surrounding cloud of objects, with a specific interest in the effect known as wave shadow, and how it affects the fusion of the pair of merging black holes. The research found that the simulation was robust to variations in the size of the cloud and the merging black holes, with some expected outcomes confirmed and others providing new insights not previously observed. The research also found that the simulation was most effective with a specific type of object known as a planetoid, with the merging black holes being drawn deeper into the cloud in their presence. The research found that the merging black holes were drawn further into the cloud in their presence, with a effect known as low velocity pushing them closer and causing a more significant disturbance of the cloud in comparison to other types of objects.

Consider an extended Euler-Bernoulli beam supported by multiple auxiliary beams, where the main beam is connected to $N$ additional beams through damping links that rotate around pivot points. All beams are interconnected via wave equations, with rotations at the pivot points governed by mechanical balance. We establish the long-term stability of this system, proving that displacements and related quantities decrease at a rate of $1/t$ as time progresses. Furthermore, if there are more than one auxiliary beams, we can ensure that solutions decay smoothly over time. Our analysis holds for any number of auxiliary beams and extends existing results in several ways, including an $N$/($N$-$1$) distinction in behavior and a consideration of initial data in a more general functional setting.

Researchers in photoacoustic tomography often encounter difficulties with the significant acoustic impedance differences between air and detection materials, which hampers the coverage of large-scale detector arrays. Although specialized matching substances exist, their high costs restrict their use in developing robust, large-scale detector systems. Researchers developed a novel lens material that effectively reduces acoustic impedance, allowing for the conversion of a wide-angle acoustic wave into a concentrated acoustic wave suitable for small detector arrays capable of scanning wide areas. When integrated with the acoustic sensor, this material enhances the sensitivity of the detector system and modifies the point spread function of the imaging system. Simulations demonstrate that this type of detector system provides enhanced sensitivity and better image resolution over a wider detection area compared to conventional setups.

Community detection is a vital issue in single network analysis that extends to multilayer settings involving the correlation between nodes across different layers. Reliant node significance captures this connection, influencing how nodes contribute to distinct communities within each layer. This paper explores prominent eigenvectors in multilayer networks to identify clustered nodes and their associated degrees of freedom. By applying this concept, we develop the Prominent Eigenvalue Community Structure (PECS) algorithm for detecting community structures in multilayer networks and evaluate its performance using both synthetic and real-world data sets. The results indicate that PECS effectively identifies macroscopic community structures, outperforming existing methods such as NMI-NetUnmix and Blocktrac. Additionally, we present the Efficient Multilayer Prominent Eigenvalue Community Structure (EMPECS) algorithm to further enhance the efficiency of computations, particularly for large-scale networks.

Our learning approach uses a collaborative framework to handle multiple degradations,
such as demosaicing, deblending and denoising, on raw images by utilizing two
connected convolutional networks and a loss function that encourages mutual
accuracy. We evaluate this method on real-world captured raw images and compare
them to ideal denoised and deblurred images obtained from in-focus photos,
showing through our results that our collaborative model's output meets or exceeds
that of sequentially using individual degradation models. Furthermore, our
experiment indicates that the collaborative method significantly outperforms
individual models in dealing with multiple degradations, notably improving
overall performance.

This study delves into the properties of a specific equation that arises from studying the Dirac equation within a generalized spacetime framework known as $R$-Minkowski spacetime. Researchers have established that this equation has a unique solution, can be consistently developed over time, and that its solution remains compact within a specific timeframe. Furthermore, certain properties of the symbol have been examined, providing insight into the underlying mathematics. Ultimately, a characteristic of the symbol's behavior at high frequencies can be deduced, showing how the dispersion surface associated with the dispersion relation can be located within a specific band in the complex plane.

This paper introduces the causal Exploration Toolbox (cET), a set of tools
for exploring high-dimensional causes and effects, with an interactive interface
that lets users efficiently identify causal relationships. By building on the DoWhy
framework, cET incorporates advanced exploration techniques and can be integrated
with existing experiments to collect and visualize data through a Matplotlib interface.
The cET is also designed with an open architecture that promotes modular growth
through the Python interface system.

This research into how nonporous spheres interact with liquid entry surface seals has been conducted for low to moderate velocity ranges, specifically between 0.13 m/s and 0.78 m/s.  A key finding from previous studies was the observation of an intermediate regime in which the seal thickness was proportional to the product of the sphere velocity and the liquid viscosity, divided by the surface tension.  However, these studies did not fully understand what determines the seal to diameter ratio in this intermediate regime.  The investigation involves analyzing the forces and pressures within the seal to better understand the seal behavior.  The results of this study into the seal geometry are confirmed by experimental evidence.  The research shows that the pressure distribution within the seal leads to higher pressures near the contact line when the seal is in the intermediate or fast regime compared to the slow regime, which is consistent with existing surface tension principles.  The study also finds that air can be trapped within the seal in a significant portion of the intermediate and fast regimes, whereas in the slow regime, the seal fully contains the air.  The finding that the pressure distribution within the seal varies depending on the seal's volume has important implications for understanding how seals of different lengths and volumes behave, particularly in the context of designing microfluidic devices.  The research also indicates that the seal geometry in the moderate speed regime can be better understood by considering the effect of the seal's volume on the pressure distribution within the seal, which has important implications for

In a broad range of Type IIB string theory effective theories, a general set of "extended theta terms" is identified that encompass all possible parity-violating coefficients affecting the fermionic and gravitational sectors of a quartic Type IIB Einstein-Maxwell-calibre theory. The study reveals that "extended theta terms" are precisely equivalent to their M-theory counterparts under Kaluza-Klein reduction. The study further develops methods to identify nontrivial "extended theta terms" resulting from compactification, particularly those arising from the moduli breakdown of M-theory superthree-form instanton effects. The study demonstrates that specific three-cycle wrapping scenarios produce unique symmetry-breaking effects within the Type IIB sector, with one such example being the unique "gravitational theta term" with no peer match in its M-theory equivalent. The study also explores how nonperturbative four-cycle breaking mechanisms influence "extended theta terms," with implications for understanding how nontrivial symmetry-breaking effects are preserved under certain limits.

Recent advances in confidence estimation for deep neural networks (DNNs) have primarily focused on analyzing the impact of training methods and specific confidence minimization techniques that utilize additional hardware resources, such as a physically isolated co-processor, to compute uncertainties. In this research, we investigate whether DNNs can inherently exhibit low confidence scores without the need for explicit uncertainty computation, solely through physical isolation of a separate processor. Our findings show that, contrary to initial expectations, certain architectures consistently produce low confidence scores across various test inputs, merely by being trained on isolated hardware. Furthermore, these architectures demonstrate superior accuracy compared to confidence-minimizing alternatives that employ extra hardware resources.

Current efforts to enhance resilient resilient autonomous driving systems have primarily focused on refining perception modules while largely neglecting the decision module's improvement. In this research, we categorize the independent resilience of the perception and decision modules into three levels based on their capacity to maintain system functions under extreme conditions. Our analysis indicates that merely relying on resilient perception methods is insufficient to prevent policy degradation due to the absence of irregular samples during training conditions. To address this challenge and elevate the indirect resilience of the decision module, we introduce a novel framework that integrates the direct resilience of the perception and decision modules. This framework also encompasses a newly developed resilient policy gradient algorithm featuring an adaptive weighting method and a severe condition identification method for the perception module, along with an innovative approach called Risk-Aware Advantage Estimation for the decision module. These contributions are further supported by experimental results involving multiple datasets and models, demonstrating the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

In the context of the box game, we analyze an variant where high-skilled players earn extra income through a selection mechanism, effectively creating a dilemma. Experimental evidence reveals that despite benefiting from this extra income, selected players tend to reduce their effort levels, whereas non-selected players increase their. Furthermore, individual characteristics such as experience, gender, and age affect how players respond to this selection-induced dilemma. Notably, we find that high-quality players can be utilized as a resource to motivate others through a form of implicit recognition.

Cubanite, a cu-Fe sulfide with a nested rock salt structure, exhibits multiple magnetic phases due to the presence of two distinct magnetic ions, cu and Fe. Experimental evidence, such as from specific heat, ac susceptibility, and x-ray absorption spectroscopy, suggests that this material may be a candidate for studying orbital-selective ferromagnetism. A theoretical analysis, utilizing full-band and DFT+U models, reveals that orbital-selective ferromagnetism emerges under certain conditions. Furthermore, this phenomenon intensifies as the Hubbard U for Fe increases, with ferromagnetic order becoming more pronounced in the occupied 3d states, potentially making cubanite an ideal material for verifying this elusive magnetic behavior.

A compelling technique to create entanglement between dark excitons in the valence band involves utilizing their bright counterparts. Here, we introduce an innovative approach based on massive electron-hole pairings within the barrier layer of a double-well structure, allowing for the generation of dark exciton superpositions that oscillate without the need for an external magnetic field. This method specifically leverages electron-spin dependent optical pairings and demonstrates that, in the absence of a magnetic field, the rate at which the dark exciton state's superposition oscillates can be adjusted by altering the electron-hole pair mass within the barrier layer. Consequently, our approach provides a highly effective and customizable means of controlling the dark exciton entanglement.

Within the 11 two-dimensional non-symmorphic wallpaper groups, there are highly versatile lattice structures that offer intriguing possibilities in lattice design, particularly in integrating multiple electronic degrees of freedom. In this study, we focus on a lattice derived from group p2m1 and incorporate multiple electronic orbital types to examine its properties, discovering that it can stabilize a Dircone within the high-symmetry route of the Brillouin zone torus. Through perturbation, we demonstrate the ability to relocate this Dircone to arbitrary positions, a capability lacking in many two-dimensional non-symmorphic group lattices. Additionally, the method of orbital inversion allows for the repositioning of Dircons throughout the Brillouin zone torus without necessitating perturbative conditions, expanding the potential for manipulating and controlling these lattice structures.

Quantum states that combine elements of both classical and quantum mechanics can be found in coherent states, which have a very strong quantum character. However, to fully explore their potential in quantum technologies, creating highly non-classical versions of these states is essential. Achieving this goal would be significantly enhanced by generating single photons that are deeply entangled. In this research, we demonstrate that using simple components, specifically linear optics, we can transform ordinary laser-light generated vacuum or coherent states into single-ph facilitated coherent states (SPICS). Our theoretical model shows that this transformation allows the output to exhibit both a very strong quantum character and both phase and amplitude modulations typical of both classical light and single photons. Interestingly, while demonstrating this capability required a moderate level of efficiency in our experimental design, we were able to show that quantum interference, a key characteristic of entangled photons, can still be observed even with lower levels of efficiency. Finally, we proposed a practical way to test the single-ph nature of the proposed method using a quantum option barrier.

In General Relativity, using the Newman-Penrose formalism provides a powerful framework for analyzing gravitational fields. This document presents an in-depth exploration of the Bivector formalism within the Newman-Penrose framework, building upon the work of Pons and collaborators. We then introduce the Bivector representation for complex electromagnetic and Weyl curvature tensors. To illustrate this representation, we derive the relevant coefficients in Pairs spinor form for the Maxwell-Weyl equations, under the assumption of a conformally flat spacetime. These derivations serve to further develop the theory and may contribute to a deeper understanding of the Bivector formalism's role in the Maxwell-Weyl equations.

Finding molecular properties using computer simulations is a common practice in chemistry. However, this approach is challenging for polymers due to the vast number of possible molecular structures they can have, particularly when considering statistical mechanics. A novel computational framework is introduced, combining linear regression and SMT solving to create a reliable method for predicting molecular properties. This deductive linear regression (DR) technique establishes a series of equivalent equations, derived from the principles of physics and chemistry, to describe the behavior of polymers. As a result, the properties of polymer systems can be understood as solutions to an optimization problem, enabling more accurate computer simulations. A basic application of this theory is explored, focusing on a polymer model consisting of interconnected harmonic springs.

Instant Transcription Enhancement (ITE) allows for real-time improvement of poor-quality audio signals, typically involving clearer speech or breathing sounds.  This paper is unique in that it addresses immediate interventions during epidemics, with a focus on breathing sounds caused by infected individuals, which can be of low quality and obscure.  A potential solution to this issue is to utilize high-quality audio signals from healthy individuals.  This research paper provides a potential framework for real-time quality improvement, with an emphasis on breathing sounds from infected patients, using real-world data.  The study explores several strategies for real-time intervention, including the use of augmented Lagrangian formalism and feasible solutions to avoid inaccuracies in audio signals.  The results indicate that these solutions can significantly enhance audio signals, with some methods achieving over 3 dB improvement in audio quality and a high level of reliability.  The research also reveals that a combination of feasible solutions and high-frequency regularization outperforms other methods, with a notable accuracy level of 97%.  The paper provides a path for future applications of real-time audio signal improvement, with a focus on ensuring public safety during epidemics.

A mixed approach of deep learning and traditional techniques has been effectively utilized in medical image analysis over the last decade. Although computer tomography (CT) scans are essential for diagnosing and treating various conditions, they can be challenging to employ for precise image segmentation due to inconsistencies in Hounsfield units and neoplasms with air pockets. One critical step in surgical intervention for patients is neoplasm segmentation, typically performed using endoscopy and/or CT scans. Based on a carefully selected dataset of 39 CT scans that include diverse types of neoplasms, we developed an original deep learning architecture called DDAUnet, which integrates novel layers for skip connection feature enhancement and pixel-wise focus. By combining this with traditional imaging methods, we demonstrated the mixed approach's superiority over sole deep learning methods for CT scans with varied textures, leading to improved overall results in neoplasm segmentation.

Our novel approach uses a flexible framework that model various distributions of rock properties across formations, from basic to complex. It assesses measurement uncertainty to create probabilistic aggregate models, providing real-time estimation of properties like conductivity and density. A case study demonstrating the development of geological frameworks, statistical modeling, and density estimation showcases the model's real-world application in a chalk field with anion-cation well logs. The framework's flexibility allows for real-time well logging analysis and real-time geosteering. Moreover, the model's modular design allows for the incorporation of machine learning-based log interpretation in the future.

Nested named entity recognition, a named entity recognition task of advanced difficulty, occurs when multiple entities within text exist in a nested relationship, one entity comprising another. Present methods address this issue by breaking it down into basic named entity recognition and binary classification. We feel these approaches fail to capture the overall text meaning, instead, we view nested entities as reflecting the holistic structure of text and propose to recognize entities through overall structure analysis. To do this, we present Holistic Matching Network, which utilizes advanced text representation and matching algorithms, incorporating pre-trained language transformation techniques like BERT and entity-specific algorithmic strategies. Our results show that Holistic Matching Network outperans other methods on two public benchmark datasets for nested named entity recognition, notably improving accuracy by at least 3.14% and 1.42% respectively.

We'll examine the connections between rational and tropical partial bitangents to a generic quartic surface in projective 3-space, highlighting their parallels in properties of dimension, multiplicity, and geometric behavior. A new family of rational partial bitangents is introduced, alongside an expansion of a previously discovered method to compute $\mathbb{A}^1$-equivalence classes of these bitangents using tropical geometry. This approach yields significant results, specifically, we will demonstrate that over a specific field of characteristics not equal to 2, $\mathbb{A}^1$-equivalence completely determines the isomorphism of bitangents. A technique to compute the signed count of real bitangents from a tropical curve is also explored, with a specific example of a family of quartic surfaces with a family of real points providing insights, ultimately leading to the discovery of a formula for the signed count of real bitangents.

This research focuses on a specific type of wireless sensor network localization technique, where the position of target nodes is calculated based on distance measurements from these nodes to several known nodes, or beacons. A significant challenge in this technique is the inaccuracy in distance measurement, particularly when measurement devices of different technologies come into contact. This phenomenon, known as cross-tech disruption, occurs suddenly and inconsistently, leading to large and random errors in measurement. A key requirement for enhancing target node localization is the design of a measurement error model that accurately describes the disruption, which is then used to develop novel distance measurement devices with improved performance. Furthermore, new, robust target node localization techniques can be created to mitigate the effects of disruption and achieve more accurate results. A comprehensive evaluation of these solutions is conducted through computer simulations and real-world experiments, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed approaches in dealing with cross-tech disruption.

This paper introduces a new perspective on multilingual code-switching Natural Language Processing (NLP), considering it a blend of language barriers and opportunities for NLPs. By representing code-switching NLP as dealing with multiple languages, it sets the stage for tackling a variety of challenges including cross-lingual text classification, sentiment analysis, and named entity recognition. To do this effectively, it is essential to account for both individual language barriers like low-resource status and complex, dynamic code-switching patterns that involve a variety of linguistic phenomena.

Human-generated descriptions of images are commonly utilized to train and evaluate image description systems. However, the systems' performance is typically assessed based on their ability to match these descriptions with the corresponding images, which implicitly presumes that the descriptions are accurate and relevant to a single image. In contrast, research has rarely considered whether the descriptions generated by humans actually reflect the content of the depicted images or simply match general consensus. This study aims to investigate whether human-generated descriptions of images truly convey accurate and relevant visual content.

Our study provides an in-depth examination of multiple configurations of the Ta$_2$O$_5$ m-phase, utilizing both first-principles and Monte Carlo simulations to validate a proposed 'base state' structure. Ta$_2$O$_5$ lies at the foundation of the tantalum capacitor industry, yet its basic crystal form has eluded full comprehension for decades. We calculated the total energy for various Ta$_2$O$_5$ arrangements, based on existing experimental data, and found the 'base state' structure to be in line with the stability range of the m-phase within the Ta-O phase diagram. This base state structure, however, predicts an Immm space symmetry, in contrast to the experimentally observed m-phase Immm symmetry. Our analysis also compared the base state structure to amorphous Ta$_2$5$ structures, as well as orthorhombic Ta$_2$O$_5$ structures, ascertaining a direct transformation path to the latter, which has recently been synthesized experimentally.

Geographic dispersion is often cited as a key benefit of the internet, with its users spread across vast distances. Recent studies have explored how physical location influences online behavior. Research has also identified how place-based dynamics affect the creation and consumption of content on platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter. Our research focuses on Reddit users who share false information and how their location affects their engagement with misinformation. Our findings reveal that Reddit members tend to upvote news from their own state more than those from other states. Geographically isolated regions with lower population densities exhibit higher susceptibility to misinformation. Our data further shows that Reddit users in rural areas are more likely to share misinformation than their urban counterparts. Moreover, our research highlights the Big Geographic Arrangement as shaping online behavior and misinformation dissemination patterns.

The escalating speed of daily news requires individuals to quickly absorb and comprehend significant events, enabling them to form informed opinions and decisions. To address this challenge, existing systems rely on low-level keyword or document-level features combined with classifiers to detect breaking stories. These approaches, while effective, require manual configuration of relevant keywords and rely on subjective term frequencies that vary across languages, contexts, and sources. In this paper, we introduce a novel, source-based method that automatically determines frequency distributions from multiple information sources, without manual configuration of relevant keywords, to distinguish between ordinary and notable occurrences. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach by presenting experimental results that show a significant improvement in detecting breaking occurrences, achieving a 15% increase in effectiveness compared to a state-of-the-art baseline system.

Humans frequently employ gestures and language when teaching skills to others. Adding this verbal and auditory component to demonstration-based learning allows a robot to benefit from verbal instructions alongside observed actions. To efficiently utilize human demonstrations, the robot must decode the connection between a human instructor's actions and spoken words. Building upon existing research, this study introduces a descriptive framework for encoding human instructors' acoustic actions, analyzing their speech content, structure, and acoustic features. Furthermore, the proposed framework is accompanied by a collection of data captured from a human instructor performing sorting and assembling tasks with a collaborative robot, including their speech. This combination provides the foundation for future studies into incorporating verbal instructions into demonstration-based learning systems.

The topological characteristics of random tree structures vary significantly
based on the probabilistic rules used to generate them. As a result, it is
generally believed that no single model can fully capture the complexity of
tree structures found in organic systems. Instead, a new approach is proposed
that encompasses multiple established generation methods within one unified
framework. This new model, called the multi-rat matrix brancher, utilizes a
distinctive multi-rat matrix to generate a diverse range of tree structures
from its single probabilistic component, thereby offering theorists a more
comprehensive theoretical foundation for analyzing organic tree systems.

From the perspective of mathematical physics, a geometric complexity in Euler-Arnold equations is equivalent to a non-uniqueness solution in geometry from differential geometry. This geometric complexity is linked to a singularity that forms in differential geometry. A specific case of this phenomenon, where an infinite curvature is created in a finite time, is identified as a "crash" in geometry. This paper delves into field theories from a geometric perspective, focusing on their inherent intricacy and potential issues of non-uniqueness. A deeper examination of the Euler-Arnold equations from Lagrangian geometry reveals a precise condition under which curvature will be generated, providing a fundamental understanding of the Euler-Arnold equations' intrinsic complexity and potential singularity formation, as well as curvature generation, within field theories.

The concept of a conversational interface, initially introduced by Turing in 1950, has been the subject of significant debate and discussion. Despite its longstanding complexity, there has been a noticeable disparity between academic research and the/conversational technology available to everyday users. To evaluate a computer's ability to engage in human-like conversation, traditional testing methods fall short due to their manual nature, subjectivity, and inability to assess the creative aspects of conversation. We have developed a novel evaluation system, Automated Assessment of Machine-to-Machine Conversation (A3MC), specifically designed to efficiently measure a conversational virtual assistant's creative capabilities by automatically generating diverse testing scenarios through human-in-the-loop algorithms.

The potential effects of a yet-to-be-discovered large trans-Neptunian object, often referred to as Planet X, on the orbital movements of the solar system's outer edges have been extensively studied.  A rigorous mathematical model is presented here which can quantify any gravitational anomaly detected while tracking the known planets from Mars out to Neptune.  The model on this present research is capable of pinpointing any unexpected forces and providing a statistical significance assessment of the identified effects.  Using this model, a specific situation is simulated where a highly elliptical and distant trans-Neptunian object would generate measurable changes in the paths of Mars through Neptune.  The results have also been compared with previous studies, and a key innovation in this work involves a novel approach in formulating the equations of motion for planetary trajectories, offering greater computational efficiency and thus enabling real-time computation.  The model presented here is groundbreaking as it is completely analytical, requiring minimal numerical calculations and can efficiently solve complex problems involving multiple celestial bodies such as the gravitational interaction between Mars and Planet X.  Given its speed, this model is suitable for implementation on mobile devices and can be utilized in future experiments designed to discover the large trans-Neptunian object.  Furthermore, the model is open-source, and its code is freely accessible on GitHub.

Neural Machine Rendering (NMR) can be thought of as extending the capabilities of Neural Machine Translation to render text into visual content. Recent breakthroughs in NMR have been made possible by employing pre-trained image-to-text models like CLIP and drawing significant NMR datasets, among them, ArtBench. However, existing solutions fall short when tackling complex tasks that require multiple model stages and unique data formats. To address this limitation, we present Monolingual Translation Archive (Mocha), a comprehensive framework capable of handling multi-modal tasks in an end-to-end manner. Mocha not only supports inference models like CLIP but also Monolingual Translation Renderer (Mochi), a novel NMR approach that utilizes existing monolingual datasets and employs a Monolingual Translation Archive (MochaRDB) to update translation models' text embeddings based on associated multilingual data and descriptive metadata. Through extensive experiments on nine tasks using Monocha, our findings indicate improved performance when comparing Monocha to baseline methods, demonstrating a format that is both user-friendly and efficient.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, known as CECCs, could reflect previous collisions between the 'anti-de Sitter boundary' and the universe's surface during the early moments following big bang. These patterns, however, are difficult to distinguish from random fluctuations due to limited observations and potential masking by interstellar dust. To address this, we develop the 'conformal diffusion' equation, which inquires about the form of fluctuations that would leave a distinctive imprint on the CECCs, ultimately affecting the observed CMB today. Moreover, we create models of 'multiverse defects' to predict their characteristics, such as how they would appear in the CECC and the Big Bang universe. Our findings suggest that defects would manifest as unusual areas in the CMB that deviate from normal fluctuations, as seen in the Cold Spot and the Quadrupole asymmetry. Additionally, we explore the impact of such defects on the formation of large-scale structures in the universe.

This paper builds upon the work of the first author and M. Tarsi, who introduced and analyzed the Yamabe evolution equation based on direct variation of a Yamabe-like energy, of which this paper continues the investigation of its convergence properties. The goal is to demonstrate the convergence of approximate solutions under more general conditions, based on existing results from previous studies. The research was funded by the ANR with grant number 19-CE40-0020.

To efficiently adapt to new tasks without retraining models, prototype-based learning uses a set of reference points. However, when the number of training examples per category is limited, traditional prototype methods fail due to distorted representations. This research proposes to generate high-quality class prototypes from abundant unlabeled data, leveraging their statistical reliability. By combining unlabeled and labeled data, the study achieves accurate prototype representations even with minimal training examples per category. Furthermore, this method can be applied to multiple existing small samples learning models, significantly enhancing their performance. Metrics like Pascal VOC 2007 demonstrate substantial gains in average precision,而出内存分类测试则显示 substantial improvements in overall and per-class accuracy.

To tackle the challenge of sparse data in multiple domains for comprehensive preference learning, a novel approach called MS-CPTRL has been proposed. This innovative method leverages cross-domain assistance to address sparse data areas and employs extensive aspect preference learning to capture implicit preferences from well-dataated regions. A significant enhancement has been introduced to aspect preference learning, enabling it to more effectively utilize well-sampled data. Furthermore, an analysis reveals that increasing the number of aspects preferentially utilizes inter-domain relationships, optimizing resource allocation and reducing potential negative influences. Extensive experiments validate the superior performance of MS-CPTRL compared to existing comprehensive preference learning methods.

Organic molecules form a vast and diverse group, making their comprehensive study a significant challenge in chemistry. To address this, researchers are utilizing high-throughput methods combined with advanced computational techniques to explore the extensive atomic combinations possible in organic chemistry. However, a major obstacle in these studies has been the use of irregular molecular representations that require complex optimization procedures. A novel approach employs convex optimization and numerical methods within a unified framework, utilizing a set of linear constraints to ensure physically plausible atomic configurations. This method enables efficient and accurate resolution of various design issues in organic chemistry, including the development of novel molecules with desired properties, the identification of stable, previously unobserved structures, and the creation of easily synthesizable molecules for large-scale analyses.

Using artificial intelligence for medical image analysis depends on the quality of training data used. Even when AI models generalize well to new scans, the underlying cause is still unclear. To better understand this, a study was conducted on AI-based assessment of Total Lesion-Asymptomatic (TLA) tumors in brain MRIs. Researchers found that AI models often appear to handle multiple scanners well, but this is usually due to them focusing on specific features or tumor sizes rather than truly generalizing. To improve true generalization to unknown scanners, better data strategies are needed. These include using models that can adapt to different types of images and avoiding bias by using better training sets. Ultimately, a thorough analysis of how AI models behave before deployment is crucial for ensuring their reliable use in medical diagnosis.

In earthquake scenarios, the reliability of the power supply network is significantly compromised, causing a substantial number of privately owned electric vehicles to lose charging capabilities. As a consequence, these EVs may still be capable of charging upon the restoration of the power supply network, which can have a substantial impact on the method and efficiency with which affected areas are rehabilitated. Therefore, it is crucial to incorporate EVs into planning for the resilience of distribution networks, with the goal of maximizing overall resilience by strategically dividing the affected areas into multiple interconnected sections. This approach, known as forming an islanding scheme, is essential to minimize the economic costs of recovering lost loads and the inability of EVs to charge, as well as to minimize the cost of repairing damaged sections of the power supply network. To achieve this, a new approach has been developed that employs decision support systems and applies game theory to model the behavior of EV owners, with each EV owner seeking to maximize their own charging success rate, with a focus on coordinating with a utility company to optimize overall system resilience. This paper also presents case studies to validate the effectiveness of this new method, which combines multi-agent optimization, with a decomposition approach, that breaks the problem down into smaller, more manageable parts, with the objective of maximizing overall system resilience by coordinating EV charging needs with the needs of the power supply network, with the ultimate goal of creating more sustainable and efficient energy systems, with a focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting energy independence, with a focus on coordinating

In cloud-based machine learning workflows and real-time stream processing, non-persistent memory modules offer a high-speed, temporary storage solution that bridges the gap between slow disk storage and limited RAM. However, their performance can vary significantly, hindering the reliable design of applications. To address this gap, many researchers use simulation models to estimate timing and throughput, although the parameters of these models often remain unspecified. This paper presents estimated parameters for several Exponential, Log-normal, and Normal-based simulation models, as well as collecting performance data for Optane DC Persistent Memory, an widely-used non-persistent memory module. Additionally, this research explores the implications of using model-based estimates over directly measuring performance data in terms of design space exploration and optimization results.

In planning a series of appointments for multiple agents moving within a given area, the primary objective for a single agent is to encourage other agents to meet with it, leveraging past behavior patterns. A solution involving agents making decisions based on historical information is proposed, where a method utilizing previous movement data to predict the behavior of other agents and encourage desired actions is presented. The approach entails formulating the problem as one of optimizing a cost function and employing a recurrent model to anticipate the movements of other agents, allowing the agent to learn the most effective strategy to achieve the desired meeting through practice. Evaluations using both simulated and real-world data demonstrate that this approach effectively achieves desired meetings with other agents with minimal need for direct communication. Furthermore, a method for efficiently executing these agents in continuous environments using implicit reinforcement learning is introduced.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within a density functional theory framework. Both anti-ferromagnetic (AFM) and ferromagnetic (FM) configurations were considered, with multiple FM configurations showing greater stability than both FM and AFM in GdSn3 and CmSn3. For the series GdxCm1-xSn3, only the most stable polymorph (II) with an FM state was further analyzed. Both FM and AFM states exhibited stability in Gd0.25Cm0.75Sn3, Gd0.5Cm0.5Sn3, and Gd0.75Cm0.25Sn3, with the former exhibiting the greatest stability. Notably, both GdSn3 and Gd0.25Cm0.75Sn3 displayed significant magnetic moments in their most stable FM states, in contrast to their nonmagnetic counterparts in other compositions.

According to the Standard Model of particle physics and contemporary cosmology, there should be equal amounts of antimatter baryons as there are baryons in the universe.  Nevertheless, observations indicate the absence of antimatter baryons on plans as wide as we can observe, creating a significant discrepancy.  As a consequence, various hypotheses have been put forth to suggest that there may be hidden forms of antibaryon and antimeson matter situated between the visible universe and the far side of the Big Bang's initial explosion.  These "dark antibaryons and mesons" would interact minimally with visible matter, allowing them to go undetected.  This paper presents forecasts for detecting such hidden antimatter using a combination of UV-collapsed gravity effects and a new form of matter called komon, which fills the space beyond the visible universe.  Consequently, there should be small regions of antimatter that can be found within the universe that could be identified through their distinctive spectral signatures.  Moreover, these antimatter regions should also produce gamma rays as they interact with visible matter.  Therefore, this study proposes that future space missions dedicated to observing gamma rays may have the capability to discover these secret forms of antimatter.

We provide a novel, simplified method to identify the fundamental sequence within a extended Coxeter group, specifically for those of type B. Our approach offers an alternative foundation for determining the group's structural properties.

Recent research has demonstrated that Type Ia supernovae visible behind galaxy clusters exhibit increased brightness due to lensing effects, potentially offering insights into the distribution of dark matter on a intermediate scale. Utilizing the comprehensive Pantheon dataset consisting of 1058 supernovae from various surveys spanning 1998 to 2014, we've undertaken a thorough analysis to identify instances of supernovae located behind galaxy clusters. After examining the data, we discovered 44 such instances, yet only 40 provided usable distance measurements. Through simulations, we determined the lensing amplification factors for these supernovae and discovered a substantial and statistically significant increase in brightness, equivalent to 16% with an error margin of 5%. Considering the confidence levels and observational errors associated with the Pantheon dataset, we estimate there to be additionally 55 such instances of supernovae located behind galaxy clusters. These estimated 99 instances represent a substantial fraction, amounting to roughly 45%, of the entire Pantheon dataset. Furthermore, these extra 55 hypothetical instances could offer valuable information regarding the intermediate scale distribution of dark matter.

These are lecture notes for a 2022 St. Flour Summer School on Stochastic Partial Differential Equations. The material covers key topics in modern research on monotone and parabolic PDEs, considering stochastic and deterministic cases, and highlights connections to singular PDEs. The lectures also introduce fundamental concepts and recent advancements relevant to these topics. The subject matter builds on established theories of function spaces, time-dependent PDEs, and rough paths.

In traditional metal interconnect technology, a critical threshold known as the Pano rate is approached, making it necessary to transition to an alternative method with higher bandwidth per power, such as using silicon photonic technology. One of the main design obstacles in photonic circuits is related to routing, especially when employing edge-coupled components, as this results in an increased footprint and potential performance issues due to higher propagation losses. A novel approach in this research involves implementing an innovative T-shaped hub in silicon photonics, which utilizes a multiplexing technique to achieve efficient routing in two dimensions and avoid wasting space, particularly when working with high-Pano rate wavelengths. Through simulations, this proposed T-shaped hub demonstrates the capability to handle up to 120G of bandwidth in a compact footprint even when metal interconnects reach their limit, thus presenting a viable solution for highly congested areas in photonic integrated circuits.

In this study, we investigate a specific issue arising from the deployment of deep learning models for medical diagnostics: various manipulation techniques can intentionally mislead these models. Our research focuses on MRI scans used to identify brain tumors, and we explore how certain image manipulation methods—specifically GANs and diffusion models—can degrade the diagnostic performance of a pre-trained neural network. Our findings reveal that, in some instances, these techniques generate highly realistic synthetic tumors that the trained network struggles to detect. Notably, we observe that GANs and diffusion models produce more subtle and realistic images, making them harder to detect than other transformation methods. Our results highlight the urgent need for further investigation and enhanced research into safeguarding medical imaging diagnostics against sophisticated attack strategies.

The algebraic framework introduced incorporates two key components: a parameter $\lambda$ within the ring $R$, and anderoand monomial map $\phi$ from the ring $R$ to another ring $A$. Within this framework, we establish that if specific conditions are met, the BernoulliCarlyle numbers $B_n(x\lambda)$ can exactly match the transformed numbers $\alpha_n=\phi(B_n(x))$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for the standard case where $\lambda=1$, various algebraic identities can be derived for Bernoulli numbers by utilizing the properties of the algebraic framework.

In astronomy, spectral analysis faces challenges due to celestial body activities across different spectral ranges that hinder empirical spectral measurement interpretation. Since these fluctuations often affect line centers in a similar manner, even a small group of spectral lines can effectively mitigate this impact. As line catalogs used for least-squares deconvolution (LSD) are increasingly extensive, choosing an optimal subset has become crucial to avoid overfitting while maximizing line density for robust pattern recognition. This study explores the effect of line selection on LSD outcomes by experimenting with line subsets featuring different characteristics. It investigates the use of line sets with random or selective line distribution across the spectral profile, as well as the impact of line catalogs with different inherent line density patterns. The study's results demonstrate that line sets with random line distribution always produce consistent and reliable LSD profiles, whereas other line selection methods occasionally yield spurious line density patterns in the residual profiles. These findings always lead to similar residual patterns when employing line catalogs with different line density patterns, whereas other methods often lead to similar residual patterns only with a line subset that has a similar density pattern. Consequently, it is suggested to use line subsets with a random line distribution for the most reliable LSD results.

This research focuses on a new method called Hierarchical Scope Sectoring (HSS) for providing integrity checks in a location integrity service, where data packets are claimed to originate from a specific place and actual location is verified. Unlike traditional methods, HSS is designed for a scenario where nodes actually located at different positions are pretending to be in the same location. It involves a source node reporting its claimed and actual positions to a central collector node, which then compares the distances between each node and the central node, as well as the angle between reported and measured signals. A statistical model is used to estimate the probability of this joint assessment being accurate. Simulation results show that the HSS method provides higher accuracy than existing methods like Triplet Range (TR) and Multi-Ranging (MR) protocols.

Recent advancements in extracting semantic context from scene images, including classified objects and their interrelationships, have made it easier for machines to grasp the core of visual recognition tasks. However, extracting detailed context from partially visible objects that extend beyond the image frame has been challenging due to a lack of visible information. Researchers have overcome this by training specialized models on extensive background context, but these systems have limited general applicability and fall short in certain contexts. In contrast, our study explores using contextual information for advanced objects detection and tracking, and we introduce a novel data set, which contains rich context from extensive region proposals related to prominent objects in everyday scenes. This is the first publicly available region context data set, suitable for cutting-edge research on objects detection and tracking. Based on the information contained in the data set, we developed a simple yet effective method to enhance the context of dense feature maps through local and contextual features. This context is less extraneous compared to typical feature maps and more informative about scene elements related to the main objects. Our context augmentation method surpasses baseline models that train on the MS COCO data set in objects detection performance, and demonstrates significant improvements with context in narrow-field-of-view narrow context data set, which is used to train the model.

This study delves into the intrinsic connections of a specific class of inhomogeneous Kirchhoff type elliptine equations, characterized by the absence of compactness and multiple unbounded negative potential wells, within an $R^N$ space, where $N\ge 3$. By employing topological arguments and variational techniques, we establish the existence of nontrivial weak solutions for this equation.

Given independent binary random variables $X_i$ taking values $\pm 1$ with
probabilities determined by parameters $p_i \in [0,1]$, the expected value $E\left(\sum X_i \mid \mathbf{p}\right)$ will remain constant as long as the number of variables with $p_i > 1/2$ and $p_i < 1/2$ stays the same, along with their respective values. It has been previously established that, under the condition that $p_i$ values are not overly spread out, concentrating the $p_i$ values at either $1/2$ or $1$ will maximize or minimize specific probabilities related to the sum of these binary random variables. In this paper, we will prove a more broad theorem that encompasses certain probabilities as convex combinations of expectations under conditioned sigma algebras, allowing us to characterize their concentration disparities as functions of their expected values. This new characterization reveals that these probabilities will share the same disparity maximum (minimum) as conditioned sums of these binary random variables.

Recently, Shibata has proposed a novel approach to extending Fontaine-Messing theory to relate K-theory over a local ring with an algebraically closed maximal ideal to the underlying geometric object's K-theory over the reduced local ring. In this study, we establish a more general relationship, which can be seen as a "foundational step" to implementing Fontaine-Messing theory over power series algebras derived from Henselian local rings. We provide a distinct proof, which may also serve as an alternative approach to replicating the results of Fontaine-Messing theory over power series algebras, extending previous outcomes found in [Can. J. Math. 43 (1991), No. 4, 528-540]. Additionally, this study offers a simpler demonstration of the results presented in [Can. J. Math. 43 (1991), No. 4, 528-540].

This paper investigates the transverse momentum dependent (TMD) correlation of two hadrons produced in sidereal deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) using a spin-polarized proton target. Specifically, we focus on the source of transverse momentum imbalance between the hadrons, particularly the dependence on the transverse momentum of the hadron moving in the opposite direction. Calculations are carried out within the factorization framework for SIDIS at four different cuts, involving longitudinal target spin, transverse momentum of the quark, and the correlation of the hadron's momentum. Our analysis includes contributions from both conventional TMD functions and higher-order twist-correct functions, impacting the cos$\phi_R$ dependence. We have also created a theoretical model for SIDIS and simulated relevant processes, using the Qiu-Schweitzer term as an example.

We've developed a method to convert Fock's 1931 4D metric into de Sitter space, achieving this through a sophisticated, non-singular coordinate transformation. This achievement aligns with 1930s-era knowledge and utilizes only established principles found in Fock's own book. Notably, we've successfully expressed the 4D de Sitter spacetime's global coordinates using a set of four simple equations, confirming that its 3D spatial slices possess a constant, positive curvature. This curvature is equivalent to the de Sitter metric's dS parameter, which can be directly related to a primordial cosmic energy density through a simple formula. Furthermore, the constant de Sitter area parameter, represented by the product of two dS parameters, can be accurately obtained from four-dimensional Euclidean geometry. This approach utilizes basic principles of Euclidean geometry to derive the de Sitter area parameter, showing that it is effectively determined by the 4D Euclidean space's intrinsic characteristics.

This research involves updating a classification of symplectic transformations, as studied by J. Walz and S. Takens, for the class of symmetric, positive-definite matrices. Two types of inner symplectic matrices are considered. We provide formulas for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the modified matrices, given the original matrices $A$ and the applied transformations $M$. These formulas are then used to demonstrate how the characteristics of definite symplectic matrices remain unchanged under $SP(2n)$-invariant modifications, ultimately leading to a revised classification.

To automatically generate entity suggestions, a new method called Wikipedia-based Diagraph Entity suggestion (WIDE) is introduced. WIDE leverages the structural information from Wikipedia to systematically convert it into various representations, then applies learning techniques to extract useful patterns that can predict entity attributes. In a thorough evaluation, using 10 different Wikipedia datasets and 1000 entity attributes for testing, WIDE outperformed the previously best entity suggestion method based on Wikipedia and showed significant improvement over this benchmark in suggested entity recall at rank 10 across nearly all entity attributes studied.

The concept of ideal compatibility in kidney transplantation is absent. 
Donors who are considered a blood type mismatch, also known as crossmatch-positive, can still provide viable kidneys to certain recipients through two methods: 
desensitization or paired kidney transplantation. 
Research was conducted to understand the factors that influence the decision of these donors to undergo transplantation, despite the blood type incompatibility. 
The study surveyed desensitization recipients and paired kidney transplant candidates, asking about their experience with the desensitization treatment, how they found out about the paired kidney transplant program, and if they had any say in the matter. 
The results showed that donors' level of involvement in the decision-making process, along with their perception of the risks associated with desensitization, played a crucial role in their decision to undergo transplantation with an incompatible kidney. 
To better comprehend the decision-making process of these donors, researchers developed a logical model using the Interpretative Structural Assessment. 
The final interpretation suggests that several main aspects influence the decision of these donors to accept an incompatible kidney, including their involvement in the decision-making process, their perception of the risks associated with desensitization, their age, their experience with the treatment, their knowledge about the paired kidney transplant program, their confidence in the medical staff, their desire to help the waiting list, their financial situation, and their interest in learning more about the procedure.

Recent advances in language understanding have been made by pre-trained models trained on vast datasets, but this training method is somewhat enigmatic. Enabling the replication of training conditions would be beneficial for comprehending how these models learn and acquire knowledge, particularly when considering the massive datasets used. One key assumption in traditional controlled experiments is that samples are independently drawn, yet in reality, they often contain inherent correlations due to the nature of natural language itself. This study explores the extent to which this assumption holds for models' learning processes. We investigate whether large-language models can be successfully trained on datasets composed of recursively concatenated sentences, effectively creating a dataset where each data point is intrinsically connected to its constituent parts. As a result, we observe that most modern language models struggle to generalize from such datasets, indicating that typical models have been adapted to exploit implicit correlations rather than developing a genuine understanding of the data. This implies that models may be exploiting shortcuts when processing natural language data, rather than truly grasping the nuances of the language itself.

This paper critically examines the common assumption that the Loughran-McDonald (LM) word list is suitable for automated textual analysis.  We investigate whether machine-learning techniques can effectively utilize the LM list, or if representation learning methods that incorporate context and textual context can more accurately capture the semantic meaning of financial language, particularly in relation to sentiment.  A comprehensive comparative study is conducted to contrast the LM-based approach with context-based and textual context-based learning models.  Surprisingly, the LM-based model shows only a minimal sentiment classification performance gain over the text-based alternative, likely due to the LM word list's inclusion of pre-classified negative and positive sentiment words.  Furthermore, we explore the potential for LM to be suited for specific subdomains or corporate types but ultimately find that context-based learning models consistently outperform the LM-based model.  The context-based and textual context-based learning models show similar clustering and performance results to advanced LM extensions, such as the LM 2D word vectors.  These findings suggest that simply enhancing the LM word vectors to capture bidirectional dependencies is insufficient, or that LM's issue lies not with the vectorization but with the LM list itself.  Given that most LM-based analyses rely on simple bag-of-words models, this study also highlights the potential for context-based and textual context-based learning models to be more effective in capturing the semantic meaning of financial language, particularly in relation to sentiment. This paper presents a method to enhance the efficiency of a multi-antenna, multi-carrier system, utilizing a novel approach to combining wideband signals and transferring data and power. Rather than relying on the common technique of equating an MISO and OFDM system to a SISO system, our method explores an alternative equivalent using scalar transmit antennas and orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (FDMA). We compare this proposed approach with the conventional method, showing that it outperforms in certain multi-antenna scenarios, yet remains a familiar and comparable equivalent to the existing system configuration.

A novel approach has been developed to address complex phenomena during the solidification and melting processes, even with multiple phases present. Building upon a previous method by Darhuber and Darhuber, which employed an embedded boundary technique for two-phase scenarios, a hybrid strategy is presented that combines this technique with a higher-level set representation. This new approach provides more flexibility in dealing with extensions beyond embedded boundary capabilities, including the breaking apart and rejoining of objects. Though primarily designed for two-dimensional problems, this method also presents a path toward solving more complex three-dimensional solidification and melting processes.

In the context of natural language analysis, a novel approach is introduced to interpret Unary Semantic Graphs. This method leverages a quantum-inspired formalism where words are represented as vectors in a directional language space, a concept known as a Dirac word. Building upon this framework, the paper focuses on examining a linguistic phenomenon called self-reference or "twisting," which occurs when a word conveys a meaning that directs another agent to interpret the same word in a different way. This is distinctly different from homonymy, as near-identical sentences can sometimes have vastly different meanings depending on interpretation paths. To model this, the authors propose introducing quantum connectors to a formalism and applying this to Natural Language Processing, a relatively new development. As a case study, they explore how a type of rhetorical figure called sarcasm can be analyzed through this lens of twisted language space, ultimately demonstrating the potential of this approach to incorporate complex linguistic phenomena into NLP systems.

In multiplayer competitions, ensuring optimal performance from participants based on their limited knowledge of others' skills is a significant challenge. Specifically, determining whether players can achieve rationalizable behavior, a basic form of strategic prediction, using a basic local information system is a key concern addressed by several established protocols. However, implementing these protocols efficiently without excessive communication overhead remains a significant issue. Our research addresses this concern by developing a new protocol that enables players to both learn each other's skills and make effective decisions using only a small amount of information. Our developed protocol does so in a relatively efficient manner, requiring a small increase in learning time but maintaining the same amount of additional communication required for players to understand each other. Our results show that this protocol performs well among players with continuous abilities, outperforming existing approaches in terms of overall effectiveness.

A Susceptible-Infected susceptible dynamics model is developed for a type of dynamic network where an isolated infected individual is identified and a susceptible individual is transferred to it, causing the connection between them to be removed. This model can be characterized as a variant of the 'soft configuration model'. Mathematical equations are derived to predict the progression of nodes that are infected or not infected over time. Furthermore, a theoretical equation is derived to describe the decay of pairs of infected nodes. Notably, this equation shows that the decay rate is influenced by second moments of degree distribution, similar to the standard SI model with protective rewiring. However, a numerical experiment demonstrates that our model predicts a significantly lower decay rate than predicted by the standard model.

In this study, we examine a type of manifold called a three-dimensional nearly Kenmotsu manifold. By introducing a Cotton soliton, we analyze its compatibility with the structure of the manifold and its associated geometry. Under specific conditions, such as when the manifold has a constant scalar curvature, we establish relationships between the potential function and the 1-form associated with the tangent field. Additionally, we prove that the manifold is conformally equivalent to a cosymplectic manifold if it satisfies certain conditions. Furthermore, we investigate the connection between the soliton's geometry and its classification within the context of a nearly Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds.

The framework of effective field theory provides a systematic method to analyze interactions, including the interaction between colorless particles and partons within high-energy hadrons or nuclei. Within this context, the effective field theory of parton distributions offers a coherent theoretical basis for processing and analyzing data, ultimately supporting new discoveries in particle physics. However, due to the complexity of hadronic or nuclear interactions, the calculations associated with PDFs are often statistically driven, allowing for the handling of large datasets, the incorporation of new data, and the exploration of theoretical constraints, including radiative corrections and various ordering prescriptions. Despite their utility, the current PDF sets lack a unified theory framework, making it difficult to compare the effective theories of quantum field theories across different models, including various PDF sets. To address this challenge, we propose an extension to the Lagrangian of quark-gluon interactions, introducing the colorless-parton sector, which encompasses the PDFs, leading to the associated equations, including the DGLAP, BK, and Glauber effects. This proposed "LEPDF" (Longitudino-Effective Quark-Gluon and Parton) extension to the quark-gluon sector serves as an extended Lorentz-Effective Field Theory, providing the necessary framework for analytically processing a wide range of data associated with partons within high-energy hadrons or nuclei.

A prominent method in the field of Deep Reinforcement Learning is combining experience replay with policy training to ensure consistent learning and efficient use of past experiences. Nevertheless, this method treats all stored experiences equally, disregarding their individual value to the policy under development. Research has shown that some past experiences can actually hinder policy improvement, having higher likelihoods of occurring simultaneously with low-value future states. This paper proposes an innovative approach, called Variance Decrease based Experience Replay (VDER), that prioritizes learning from experiences with lower probabilities of co-occurrence. By introducing a method to estimate the probability of such experiences and incorporating it with the legal action space, we can identify and downplay the influence of these unnecessary correlations, ultimately accelerating policy convergence and minimizing the need for extensive exploration. The effectiveness of VDER has been demonstrated through comparative evaluations on various continuous control benchmarks and a game-based test, showing significant convergence and performance enhancements when used in conjunction with the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm.

The pycommute library is a Python module designed for working with operator algebras used in many-body quantum systems research, extending the C++ 'libcommute' engine for symbolic computation. It covers a range of algebraic operations and can be applied to models like the transverse field Ising model while supporting abstract algebraic abstractions, including tensor products and symmetry-based derivations, with integration into SymPy for user-friendly Python syntax, and extensive tests through pytest, and comprehensive documentation via pydoc.

Within the pseudogap region of hole-doped cuprates and cuprate-based cuprates, the phenomenon of electronic order is observed in some studies but remains elusive in others. In contrast, the nature of barium strontium copper oxide exhibits consistent evidence of in-plane charge order within its pseudogap region. By analyzing bare mass spectra and spatial correlations using scanning tunneling microscopy, we establish that the charge order in barium strontium copper oxide is genuinely two-dimensional. Moreover, we demonstrate that above the superconducting state, a distinct superconducting void is created where the charge order persists. These observations provide robust evidence of authentic two-dimensional electronic order in barium strontium copper oxide.
