Within the Rashba Hubbard model featuring spin-flip mechanisms from the attractive variant, we have demonstrated that a topological superfluid phase with spin-singlet characteristics can arise. Firstly, we utilized the Gutzwiller mean-field theory to reveal that RSH exhibits intrinsic time-reversal-breaking order parameters responsible for spin-singlet pairing dynamics. Furthermore, our findings indicate that, in adequate frameworks where Rashba spin-orbit coupling exists, Rashba terms do not override the competing exchange interaction, thus allowing for spin-singlet pairing within the simplified standard Hubbard model.

By using highly sensitive, gradient-based magnetometry, we have detected the characteristics of vortex lines and grids within a superconductor of doped bi-cuprate, $\textrm{Bi}_2\textrm{Sr}_2\textrm{CuO}_4\textrm{ (+i)}$, as we vary the applied magnetic field. Specifically, we have resolved the volume fraction and shape of individual vortex lines and grid cells inside the superconductor sample, as we have mapped the first-order transitions of vortices from isolated lines to square grids in two distinct orientations, perpendicular and diagonal, relative to the crystal lattice lattice. This is observed to occur at very close $B$-field values for these transitions, occurring perpendicular and at significantly higher $B$-field values, diagonal and relative to the $a-b$ crystal lattice.

A previously unexplored phenomenon occurs at the edge of a polymer brush where the structure transitions abruptly, an effect attributed to entropic forces in densely packed regions and remains controversial due to the assumption that solvent molecules are excluded completely from these regions. In this study, we examine elongated brush ridges consisting of molten polymer chains by utilizing inhouse experimental data and advanced computer simulations, an approach enabled by the relatively short relaxation times. Entropic forces are balanced with surface and polymer-wall entropic forces to derive conditions for complete edge exclusion and a sizeable volume within the edge region where the melt phase dominates. Additionally, we show that elongated brush ridges naturally develop into various shapes, some of which exhibit edge exclusion while others do not, based on their geometry. Our research provides a fundamental understanding of edge regions in polymer brushes of all types and designs, based solely on design parameters of the surface.

Given a graph G and a subset S of its vertices, we say S resolves x in G if for any two distinct vertices u and w in G, the path lengths from x to u through elements of S differ from the path lengths from x to w through elements of S. A subset S of G is called a metric dimension if it resolves all pairs of vertices in G. Recently, a concept known as shortened metric dimension was introduced as a variant of the traditional metric dimension, specifically defining a subset S that identifies at least one pair of vertices in a graph based on shorter paths rather than the usual shortest paths. In this paper, we explore and define properties of shortened metric dimensions on various types of finite graphs, including paths, cycles, complete graphs, and several compound graphs. Additionally, we introduce lower bounds for the shortened metric dimension of binary trees and n-vertex grids.

A machine learning technique was employed to analyze high-precision spatial and spectral data from the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, specifically 2-year Global Map and a diverse range of individual source spectra. Initially, support vector classification and linear support vector regression models were tested for their accuracy in reproducing energy density spectra from photons. After optimizing hyperparameters, the algorithm significantly enhanced the match between observed and modeled data, reducing residual errors by a factor of three to four compared to traditional fits. When applied to the 2-year Global Map, this machine learning approach also improved the match, reducing squared residual errors per degree of freedom by approximately  twenty percent. Furthermore, the model identified around  five more variable sources on average, although the additional sources had lower statistical significance, around  three times, than the confirmed sources. -
