A new linearity test has been created for network autoregressive models, with the test statistic's asymptotic distribution analyzed under different scaling conditions for elements of the provided adjacency matrix. The result leads to a linearity test based on the comparison of two estimates - linearity and nonlinearity - and an alternative approach using linearity identification has been introduced. For the purpose of demonstration, a Monte Carlo study has been conducted to evaluate the test's performance. Additionally, an application example was used to show the test's effectiveness in a real-world scenario.

In recent years, declarative networks have gained significant attention due to their ability to combine the advantages of generative and discriminative models, while mitigating their respective drawbacks. In this work, we introduce the concept of Issue Framework, a novel theoretical foundation that can facilitate a deeper understanding and more versatile application of declarative models. By issuing two key requirements, the Issue Framework issues, we compel declarative models to effectively address the benefits and issues associated with generative and discriminative models. As an response, we provide an in-depth examination of two representative declarative models, namely Disentangled Declarative Networks and Declarative Variational Autoencoders, in essence, analyzing their ability to issue Model Equivalence and Information Reuse. Furthermore, our work includes micro and macro perspectives on the Issue Framework's issues, encompassing theoretical underpinnings, practical implications, and philosophical inquiries, along with an expanded perspective on research directions for future models.

A new, open-source Python library has been developed for Hele-Shaw flow simulations with active substances. It allows for the modeling of cellular dynamics and lipid membrane behavior by incorporating approaches like particle-based, phase-field, and front-tracking methods. The library will be demonstrated through parallel simulations of Hele-Shaw flow and cell motility, and made available on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11.particle-based, -phase-field-, and -front-tracking-approaches-to-cellular-dynamics-and-lipid-membrane-behavior-. It was contributed by researchers from the University of Oxford, including J. Brash, J. Smith, J. Rudnicki, J. Oshkoe, J. Humphrys, and J. King, as well as the University of Edinburgh's School of Informatics.

Crypto scams, also known as cryptocurrency fraud, involve deceptive behavior on cryptocurrency platforms that deceive victims into believing they are making profitable transactions, ultimately costing them substantial sums of money. Researching cryptocurrency fraud is challenging due to limited openly available data from real cases, as criminals keep their financial trails concealed to avoid detection. To address this limitation, researchers have developed synthetic datasets to study the characteristics of these scams, but they lack real-world currency traversal data. In response, a new approach called Currency Traversal Graph (CTG) has been created by extracting transaction histories from actual scammed wallets on the Ethereum blockchain, providing transaction traversal graphs for use in future research on detecting and identifying these scams. Initially, a preliminary detection model based on CTGs is presented in this paper, but its performance is hindered due to the high complexity of currency trails, underscoring the need for further investigation into actual scam detection methods. Furthermore, to facilitate future research, a public dataset containing this currency traversal graph is made available on Amazon S3, along with associated code accessible on GitHub.

Quantum optimal control techniques effectively address issues of imperfect quantum hardware, but their sophisticated mathematical principles may be imperfectly executed by experimentalists, resulting in failures even when the executed protocol is optimal. This study presents a machine learning approach that generates robust quantum circuits by training a reinforcement learning agent to choose both the parameter values and application timing of controllable components in open-loop feedback systems. Reinforcing the learning agent based on the error rates of the final quantum state enables the emergence of an effective, implicitly optimized schedule for applying the controllable components, eliminating the need to manually design temporal sequences. Utilizing simulation models, we demonstrate the proposed method's error reduction benefits for both pulse-level and logical quantum error mitigation.

Precise timing and frequency measurements are being transformed by single photons that travel through optical circuits, as they can significantly amplify small changes in these signals. Notably, a single photon in a setup where it can take on multiple paths at once, such as in an interferometer, shows the most sensitivity to variations in travel times. This work presents an innovative approach called 'quantum double leap metrology', involving two linked cavities, that allows for precise measurement of small differences in cavity lengths using only the single photon. By 'store-and-compute' data from each separate path, this method beats the usual accuracy limits and can equal the performance of more complex setups utilizing many particles. Moreover, it outshines previous methods using a single photon in terms of accuracy.

The PHENIX collaboration examined the dependence of photon-hadron correlation data on transverse momentum in 200 GeV/A Au$+$Au, $d$$+$Au collisions. A significant suppression was observed for Au$+$Au collisions when the hadron $p_T$ surpassed 5 GeV/$c$, a trend not seen in $d$$+$Au collisions. This study further analyzes the dependence of this suppression on the central rapidity and longitudinal distribution of Au$+$Au collisions. Evidence points to medium interactions as the cause of this suppression, with a similar result seen in $d$$+$Au collisions regardless of hadron type, supporting the notion that jet-medium interactions drive the suppression of data.

In 2006, Prof. W. Smarandache introduced the concept of the Smarandache sigma multiplication of digits, identifying the first few instances where the equation holds true, including notable cases of 25, 104, 108, 112, 128, 136, 144, 153, 160, 168, 176, 184, 192, 208. This paper presents a general framework for determining all possible integers that can be expressed as the universal Smarandache sigma multiplication of digits for any number of digits, and additionally, it establishes at least 6 more integers that satisfy this universal property.

The multi-tiered sound architecture, featuring front-end clusters and a cloud of backend servers coordinated by a global load balancer, has become a popular design for latency-sensitive applications due to its ability to scale horizontally and improve reliability. However, achieving high availability and scalability within this architecture poses significant challenges, especially given the inherent network variability across its network components. Our research on the Google Search architecture revealed that even minor network fluctuations can lead to significant drops in backend availability, affecting as much as 30% of services and up to 70% of instances. To address this issue, we introduced a set of guidelines for maximizing scalability in cloud services built using the sound architecture, emphasizing the importance of network efficiency in load balancing and application design. Our case studies on Google Search and Cloud Todo demonstrate that following these guidelines can result in a tenfold increase in scalability. Furthermore, we proposed a set of cloud load balancing techniques aimed at maintaining network efficiency, integrated into the B4 algorithm. By adopting these strategies, developers can potentially avoid unnecessary cloud costs while maintaining high availability.

We examine a scenario where multiple learners participate in the same situational linear context with a distinct but unknown goal, and where the available data is insufficient for them to discover the target goal alone due to inherent exploration-exploitation tensions. A key characteristic of this setup is that a new learner can leverage knowledge from previous participants by sharing their experiences, while maintaining independence from them. We investigate shared learning algorithms that utilize either a parametric or non-parametric approach, and explore how they leverage past data to achieve better performance than standalone learning methods. In particular, we develop a novel shared algorithm under a setting of perfect information transfer and develop methods to account for imperfect information that involves either overwriting or accumulating the data. A theoretical analysis of these methods reveals relevant regret bounds in terms of exploration, inheritance, and exploitation errors. A numerical experiment on an image classification task demonstrates the advantages of the proposed methods over conventional explored-free shared algorithms.

Over the years, the prevalence of remote working has risen sharply and its impact on the successful completion of projects utilizing the Scrum framework remains largely unknown. This research undertakes a comprehensive examination of how remote working influences the achievement of Scrum-based projects, combining theoretical concepts with empirical evidence. To complete this investigation, a combination of quantitative and qualitative data was collected, starting with a survey administered to 300 professionals who have experience working on Scrum projects, followed by in-depth interviews with 17 participants. The results of the research were then integrated through a combined statistical analysis and theoretical modeling. This study's findings provide unique contributions to the existing body of knowledge by offering both practical advice for organizations transitioning to remote working and a deeper understanding of how Scrum functions across geographical boundaries.

We appreciate the interest shown by Rao, Zhang, and Hu our work on Distributionally Robust Individualized Treatment Guidelines (DRITG). Physicians using standard medical treatments may be susceptible to subtle systemic influences that can adversely affect patient outcomes, a problem highlighted by Suominen, Draper, and Hu in recent studies. To address this issue, we developed a new framework, the DRITG, which considers multiple possible distributions and seeks for a treatment that minimizes the worst possible distribution-specific risk, a novel contribution to the broader field. Our initial findings indicate that the DRITG can effectively prevent external inconsistencies while maintaining comparable performance to the idealized standard treatment guidelines. Upcoming research should explore various robust risk measures, such as those used in robust optimization, and develop more sophisticated deep learning models to better capture complex data patterns. In response to specific comments from reviewers, we have updated our code and conducted additional analyses, which we have made publicly available for further use by other scientists in the field.

Our analysis of the event shape engineering (ESE) technique at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) reveals a limitation in its applicability for detailed study under high-energy conditions. By examining the event activity shape in lead-lead collisions at the LHC with a center-of-energy mass of 2.76 TeV and an integrated luminosity of 0.1 nb^-1, we found that certain activity metrics, such as those derived from the track-TPC, can influence elliptic flow coefficients (v_2) in p_T. However, this effect is minimal. Consequently, ESE may not be an optimal approach for exploring the quark-gluon plasma's properties at high energy. Furthermore, we explored possible drivers behind the observed track-TPC influence on v_2 and found that their average multiplicity can account for nearly all of the effect. Since increasing the track count has a negligible impact on the lead-lead collision's initial geometry, we conclude that for high-energy investigations, focusing on other types of activity measures with a more significant impact on v_2 may be more effective.

This paper introduces the concepts of orthogonality and Parseval's identity associated with the quaternion linear canonical Fourier transform, and examines the ambiguity, phase retrieval, and Zakar-Kolmogorov-Schwinger identities for the transform.

This research builds upon previously established results indicating that utilizing optimal power control methods over binary power regulation can significantly enhance GDoF achievement in well-balanced interference networks by a factor of approximately $\Theta(K^{1/2})$. Nevertheless, no corresponding studies have assessed the impact of employing optimal power control methods compared to simple binary power regulation on extremal, unbalanced networks. We establish the extremal unbalanced case where the desired GDoF benefit over binary power regulation, when the strongest user is considered, scales as $\Theta(K^{1/2})$. Furthermore, we determine the extremal unbalanced configuration in which the desired GDoF for all users when applying binary power regulation reaches its maximum. Analyzing various unbalanced scenarios, we discover that the extreme unbalanced case with one user experiencing two interference signals with a factor of two difference in power, while the remaining $K-3$ users share equally divided interference, represents an local minimum.

In particle-resolved computational simulations, determining the exact moment particles collide can significantly impact them. To accurately capture this interaction and the resulting changes in the fluid, the simulation must have a small time step, which can impede them due to the vast number of particles involved, particularly in long-duration simulations. To circumvent this limitation, researchers have developed methods to use larger time steps, enabling them study the relationship between particles and them over extended periods. One such method involves updating the position and velocity of particles based on their current state and the colliding particle's state at different points in time, thereby avoiding the need to calculate collisions in real-time. This paper builds upon a statistical approach to capturing collisions and demonstrates that updating states in batches can accurately capture short-term particle dynamics and reduce the error when compared to resolving collisions with a traditional direct simulation.

This article provides $2$ distinct proof methodologies establishing the existence of pairs of relatively prime whole numbers, $a$ and $b$, for any given positive whole number, $n$, such that the expression $a^2+ab+b^2$ equals $7^n$.

To enable robotic devices such as legged locomotion systems to traverse difficult and soft surfaces, it is crucial to model the surface properties accurately. One effective method for creating suitable surface models is using viscoelastic foundation elements (VEFE) that simulate forces like friction, inertia, and damping. By incorporating a VFE model into the dynamics of a simple one-legged jumping robot, we can develop a precise model of its movement on surfaces. This allows for the evaluation of jumping techniques and testing of new control methods. In this study, we developed a rolling hop jumping trajectory and controlled it using multi-phase feedback feedback linearization (MPFL). The results showed that the current control system produces longer jump distances than a previous system, even on difficult surfaces, without sacrificing stability. The findings of this research may contribute to the successful design and operation of more advanced walking machines capable of navigating difficult terrain.

In a new theoretical framework, we derive the meson's charge and magnetic moments, as well as the flexibility of its shape, for both quarkonia and non-quarkonia. Our approach, based on a cohesive quark-antiquark model, allows for the consistent description of these phenomena and various flexible models yield the same magnetic moment formulas. Furthermore, we apply this cohesive scheme to explain the observed flexibility of quarkonia and hadronic flexibility in non-quarkonia systems, such as the $\pi^+$, $K^+$, $D\pi$ and $B^\ast D$ mesons.

Historically, observations of the droplet electrohydrodynamic fan phenomenon in liquids have been supplemented by empirical data, but understanding the underlying mechanisms through theoretical means in liquids remains limited. However, when investigating dry systems, particularly sand, numerous theoretical explanations have been put forward. This study puts forward a novel, streamlined theoretical model specifically tailored to explain the mechanisms at play in the exhibition demonstrated during the 2023 AIAA/CEAS 23rd European Conference on Aerospace Sciences where liquid droplets form a fan-shaped pattern. The model's accuracy is validated against experimental data, revealing that previously successful theoretical explanations for dry systems cannot accurately predict the patterns observed in this liquid-based experiment.

Recent advances in natural language generation have yielded systems capable of producing high-quality outputs, yet evaluating their interpretative capabilities remains a challenge. Evaluating comprehensiveness, particularly in systems generating multiple contradictory options, poses even greater difficulty. In this study, we introduce a novel assessment method for evaluating systems that generate contrasting interpretations, specifically in the context of negational reasoning. Our approach involves presenting multilingual readers with articles containing deliberate contradictions and asking them to select the most accurate interpretation, along with a non-contradictory one, from a set of provided options. A diverse range of human-generated answers have been collected, along with an initial set of machine-generated results, which we analyze to determine key factors influencing machine interpretational success. Our findings reveal that semantic similarity plays a crucial role in prioritizing non-negational interpretations, whereas pragmatic coherence appears to be the deciding factor for negational interpretations. Furthermore, we explore the potential for using human and machine-compressed representations to effectively rank multiple contradictory interpretations, thus demonstrating the efficacy of this method.

Current methodologies for deriving hierarchical structures, such as MAAPO and AMAP, have been effectively tested but lack expansion opportunities. These approaches employ an optimization-based framework to determine subsets of attributes within predefined subsets of objects, but this method has limitations. Since these methods do not incorporate the concept of irreducibility, they risk generating duplicate outcomes and fail to satisfy certain application requirements, such as those in multi-criteria decision analysis. Although some alternative methods have been proposed, they come with their own set of drawbacks, including the absence of an attribute centrality score, the use of heuristics, or the lack of an established mathematical foundation. In response, we introduce a novel approach to obtaining an entire hierarchy of pre-ranked subsets of objects, defined by their contentment with a specific set of attributes, utilizing the same mathematical foundation as the current best method but with an added set of mutually non-intersecting criteria, thus enabling a more comprehensive outcome.

Quantum annealing is generally considered to behave like a quench process due to its essential component, the tunneling effect, interacting with a continuously changing landscape. 
Taking into account this duality, we develop and analyze a time-dependent quench Hamiltonian derived from a precise cover formulation, where the problem parameters are separated into static and dynamic components. 
Through studying the probabilities of the system's states after the quench, our results reveal signatures of residual charge and fractionalization, as well as cases of partial cover, no cover, or multiple solutions. 
These findings offer new insights into the nature of quantum annealing and have significant implications for the design of annealing protocols, particularly for D-Wave systems. 

In summary, our study demonstrates the equivalence of the precise cover problem to the Fermi-Hubbard model and establishes a framework for understanding quantum annealing in relation to the ferromagnetic Ising model. 
Our results imply that, unlike the Fermi-Hubbard model, quantum annealing does not exhibit spontaneous symmetry breaking, providing valuable insights into the development of efficient programming protocols for these systems.

In recent years, industries such as aerospace and automotive have increasingly relied on maintenance activities based on historical data and operational experience. One method they use involves identifying common patterns in flight traces from aircraft that have undergone specific maintenance checks, comparing them to new flights and deciding when to perform more in-depth inspections. This process of matching patterns, whether by inserting elements or removing others, known as alignment, helps identify similarities between different sequences. This study explores using alignment techniques, specifically infix and postfix alignment, to improve current conformance verification methods for partial traces. It also presents new approaches called aligned prefix verification and the combination of infix and post-fix verification to ensure the safety of trace 'segments'.

To determine the screening capability and carrier type within infinite-layer nickelate NiNiO_O, we employed time-reversal symmetry to analyze its optical properties and extend the Drude-Lorentz model to infinite systems. Calculations of many-body spectral functions using the MAXIM algorithm revealed that the screening behavior can be accurately represented by the combined effect of screening by high-frequency spins and shorter-distance electrostatic forces. The results indicate the existence of an intrinsic screening length of approximately 5.3 Å, beyond which charge screening becomes negligible. Our study also reveals that to effectively screen an external electric field, carriers must supply approximately 2e per unit area. Moreover, the calculated screening length of approximately 3.4 Å using the MAXIM spectral function contrasts with the fitted value of approximately 7.1 Å observed from the optical conductivity. Notably, within the visible spectrum, the material exhibits strong light absorption due to its relatively short screening length.

This paper addresses the long-range Boltzmann equation with hard potentials under non-cutoff assumptions in infinite space. By considering initial data differing significantly from equilibrium under a uniform divergence condition, we have proven new local and global well-posedness results. Specifically, we have developed an approach that integrates the relative factorization technique with a novel divergence condition to establish solution stability. This method led to two key findings. Firstly, we have obtained a local well-posedness result under a divergence condition with no requirement for smallness of the initial data. Secondly, under an additional boundedness condition, we have established the corresponding global well-posedness property. These results have united two previously distinct approaches in a more unified framework for understanding the long-term behavior of solutions to the Boltzmann equation.

We used Advanced Sounder for Initial Satellite Appraisal (IASI) radiometer data to measure the brightness temperature of the Earth's atmosphere and the ocean surface, from 2007 to 2014, which helped us study wave characteristics on the Mediterranean Sea, North Atlantic Ocean, and South China Sea. By applying a theoretical model of wave crests, we calculated mean square wave heights and mean wave slope angles. To ensure the reliability of our results, we used resampling techniques to control for temporal and spatial autocorrelation in the data. Our analysis revealed that wind speed could be accurately predicted using regression models based on wave height and slope angles, with a mean error rate of 0.43 m. Notably, a simple model using only wave slope angles yielded the lowest error. The complexity of sea wave crests can vary by location, as shown by random forest importance measures, which indicated that wind speed was the primary factor contributing to wave structure, accounting for up to 50% of variability. This variability could also be attributed to variations in atmospheric humidity and pressure, each contributing as much as 10%. Our results revealed that sea waves in calm conditions (up to 8 Beaufort) maintained a level of symmetry comparable to that of the ocean in more turbulent conditions (above 8 Beaufort), which exhibited varying levels of skewness across the range of wind speeds.

Large-scale software frameworks are critical in accelerating the development of software frameworks by providing framework structures and requiring comprehensive testing and validation. The testing and validation of sophisticated software frameworks often require a significant investment of time and money. To address this issue, a test scenario selection algorithm based on UD is proposed to determine whether the current set of tested code paths can fully cover the framework's logic structure. A parallelized version of this algorithm is also proposed, aiming to enhance the time efficiency of the calculation without compromising its precision. Furthermore, the authors conduct a series of experiments using the CMAKE software framework to evaluate the performance of the parallelized algorithm, and the results show that the parallelized algorithm can significantly improve the time efficiency of the calculation when dealing with larger datasets.

Social media platforms can reveal public sentiment during major global crises, which can influence the spread of diseases like COVID-19. Analyzing the emotional tone of people's posts during such events is essential for tracking the progression of a pandemic. To research this, we need to efficiently extract emotional content from a large amount of data, but existing tools are often inadequate for dealing with the vast amounts of information in multiple languages. In an effort to overcome these obstacles, we created a comprehensive Chinese and English microblogging dataset called WeiboCor20, which includes the emotional content of people's posts during the initial phase of the pandemic. Our analysis of this dataset revealed distinct clusters of opinion groups based on their emotional state, which shifted over time. Furthermore, our research revealed that emotional assessment models perform better in microblogging datasets compared to Twitter data, likely due to differences in user demographics and data characteristics.

Integrating all available experimental evidence, we re-examine the interlayer conduction mechanisms in cuprate superconductors. Our analysis considers a two-dimensional copper oxide layer conduction and the coupling between these 2D layers in multiple cuprate families. Utilizing established models for 2D conduction, we investigate how charge density wave patterns influence coupling between layers, and we find these models consistently apply across cuprate families. These conclusions are supported by both theoretical computations and experimental measurements of interlayer conduction properties.

Theoretically, the sound speed in dense matter should drop below the neutron star density due to electronic pressure constraints, yet some models foresee its increase in density, particularly those involving quark matter, by rising from the typical nuclear pressure of $c\approx0.5$ to the universal limit of the speed of light. Observations of neutron stars suggest very high pressure could exist within their cores without contradicting observations. Consequently, the fundamental limit on sound speed may not apply to the dense matter found in neutron star cores. Instead, two distinct limits on the sound speed may instead govern the matter: one, approximately $0.5c$, exists in density within the nuclei of matter, while the other limit, potentially removing a strict constraint on the sound speed, could instead exist beyond this density.

Xi, Zhang, and Wang previously developed a comprehensive method to create ordered tree structures from designated sequences of closed pairs and individual elements, and subsequently, Li and Wang applied this method to generate sorted forest structures. Our research introduces a straightforward and universal method to generate reversed counter pairs from unordered tree structures while maintaining the underlying structure's shape, and applies this method to produce reversed Tai mappings for unordered labeled arborizations. Our approach is more direct and more widespread than the previous method, addressing limitations where the previous technique only worked for specific subtypes of unordered tree structures with no single elements.

This research employs the 10-elem commass basis to analyze the effects of coordinate compression and shifting on the Fock space. By applying a unitary transformaton, we investigate how these modifications expand or reduce the 10-slem set's orthogonality and completeness within the Fock space. The study reveals that, generally, the compressed-shifted 10-clem set lacks full rank in the 10-slem set, indicating that some phonon states cannot be reached from their compressed versions. Specifically, it is demonstrated that in the microscopically compressed set, where the compresssion coefficient meets the inequality $|\beta| \leq 1$, the impact of shifting vanishes at infinite shell numbers. The comass system's basic principles are explained, including its application to the issue of phase invariance in the seniority-0 su(4) collective Hamiltonian.

A vertical shear instability is proposed to be a potential issue for dust particles overcoming the barrier of meter-sized. An investigation was undertaken to explore its impact on the growth of these particles, taking into consideration rotation forces and a condition known as Keplerian. It was discovered that disk stability is influenced by both dust viscosity and shear thickening, as well as the mass of the central star, with some disks becoming turbulent due to reduced effectiveness of dust suppression on stability, with further meter-sized barrier crossing possible in these cases, as highlighted by T-SSC T-RRA results, with some extending to boulders, with potential connections to observed large astrosilicate features, with some attributed to photoevaporation outflows as well, with some potential connections to circumstellar dust clouds found in some systems, with some attributed to photoevaporation outflows as well.

This research paper establishes a Liouville theorem for manifolds with specific Ricci curvature restrictions and constant scalar curvature, with the main result indicating that under certain conditions on nonlinear equation solutions, the solution must be constant. A specific application of these findings involves proving that complete Stefan-Sagier manifolds with uniform bounds can have a bounded fundamental solution. The paper's results build on previous work by Donaldson and Topping regarding the heat equation on parabolic manifolds.

Recently, the FARE framework stands out as a prominent and comprehensive framework for advanced entrance systems, integrating diverse techniques like representation learning and hashing to reduce the length of user logins. Although these methods have achieved impressive results in accelerating authentic logins, their performance in detecting suspicious activities during initial logins remains limited. This paper introduces two novel methods, named EArH and DynamicFairNet, that not only enhance the efficiency but also maintain strong security during initial logins. EArH integrates representation learning and anti-bias strategies in the hashing network, whereas DynamicFairNet adapts a dynamic attention-based attention mechanism to balance the data and network's imbalance. Our experiments on the CAISSA15 dataset demonstrate that both models outperform existing benchmarks in terms of accuracy and anomaly detection during initial logins.

Within general relativity, measuring the distance to nearby celestial objects using astrometry is influenced by gravitational time delays and light bending in a way that aligns with the Parameterized Post-Newtonian framework. Our calculations indicate that for typical nearby objects, the relevant effects are so small that they won't significantly impact the precision of parallax measurements achieved by missions like Gaia, despite the uncertainty in the gravitational parameter $\gamma$. The impact of $\gamma$ on parallax is found to be about 5 orders of magnitude smaller than the impact of $H_0$'s uncertainty, which can be understood through the vast difference between local and cosmic scales. The relevant effect in the Hubble flow can be attributed to the extraordinary vastness of this flow compared to typical local scales.

The complexity of modern systems demands a simplified model for effective simulation, analysis, and control, without compromising the accuracy of the system's essential behavior. This paper presents a simple and efficient method to create a reduced-order model for a nonlinear dynamic system, based on identifying a minimal subset of state variables that capture the system's primary characteristics. The algorithm utilizes the system's input and output data to find the underlying linear or nonlinear relationships, resulting in a significantly smaller model with a fraction of the original states, as demonstrated with a nonlinear chemical reactor and a helicopter model, providing a practical and effective approach to system simplification.

A novel class of objects known as self-boosting solitons (SBs) is identified within relativistic rotating fluids in three dimensions, representing self-accelerating self-sustaining solitons. SBs exhibit self-generated boost through anisotropic pressure gradients aligned with self-generated centrifugal forces in rotating frames of reference. The properties of SBs are closely aligned with those of perfect fluids in the sense that they utilize the equation of state for ideal fluids to describe their rapidly expanding behavior. The self-generated centrifugal force arises from the interaction of the fluid's rotation and its equation of state, allowing SBs to describe the equation of state interaction through their unique self-boosting characteristics.

To overcome the limitations of existing secure machine learning methods that prevent a server from being tempted to cheat, this paper introduces a novel approach called差别化隐私保护训练客户端 (SIMC). SIMC is an improvement over the original technique, which involved a secure training process and a differential transformation process. The original SIMC achieved a certain level of accuracy, but it required significant computational resources and took a long time to complete. The new SIMC achieves a much higher accuracy of 0.9383, while reducing the computational requirements and completing the process in less than 0.5 minutes, all while using standard, off-the-shelf components, including a standard GPU.

The radio telescope known as FAST has a sensitive sensitive capability to observe the 21-cm hydrogen line, and the discovery of previously unknown HI features has been made possible. In this work, using the same 1.1 GHz bandwidth data, we have identified a total of 14 distinct HI entities, including 6 entire galaxies already known. Additionally, we have found a cluster of gas clouds located near IC 4329, as well as a tail of hydrogen extending from IC 4594 as it orbits around NGC 5979. These features highlight the potential for FAST to significantly expand our understanding of galaxies and the universe as a whole.

To handle the vast amount of potential answer combinations in the Question Answering (QA) challenge, our research centers on capturing the semantic context in responses from both questioners and candidate answerers, as well as in the knowledge being utilized. We introduce a novel approach, called Semantic-connected Insight (SemIns), to tackle this issue in open-domain QA. This approach combines a multi-task neural network that cures data inconsistencies and enhances knowledge exploitation, along with a knowledge-graph-based verifier that ensures factual accuracy in the reasoning process. We evaluate SemIns on the CommonsenseQA dataset and outperform current top-performing methods, improving both performance and interpretability in the QA process.

The recent discovery of multiple species, including OH^+, CN^+, and CN^+H, in the coma of 47/52P/Asteroid has highlighted the necessity of in-depth analysis of the coma's spectral features. While some of these species can be easily observed using existing technology, the current models for predicting their behavior are based on simplified assumptions, primarily due to a lack of comprehensive data on the reactions involving these molecules. The formation and destruction mechanisms for oxygen-containing molecular cations in the coma of 47/52P/Asteroid are still not fully understood, limiting our ability to accurately predict their observed concentrations. The situation is particularly acute for larger molecules consisting of multiple atoms, where the formation of these molecules through the process of recombination is only observed in a couple of instances, despite their significant role in determining the concentrations of these molecules. The current study delves into the complexities of these molecules' behavior in the coma, highlighting the need for in-depth analysis of their formation and destruction mechanisms, as well as the limitations of existing models for predicting their concentrations. The article emphasizes the critical role of these molecules in determining the coma's spectral features, while also discussing some of the challenges associated with their study.

The study investigates the representability of integers as sums of values taken by certain algebraic expressions across various mathematical domains, specifically focusing on quadratic and cubic forms. The primary method used in this study involves applying results from a recent paper by Beeker and Vaintrob regarding totals in certain algebraic structures. These results, which are particularly useful for large values, can be somewhat limited in application to fields. However, more expansive domains, which include but are not limited to the set of integers, offer more meaningful applications for these findings. The study proves that every sufficiently large integer can be expressed as the sum of four values taken by a certain quadratic form, which represents a significant contribution to a longstanding problem first discussed by Heegner in 1953. The study also proves that every sufficiently large integer in a certain algebraic number field, which has certain properties, can be expressed as the sum of four values taken by a certain quadratic form, thus resolving a problem posed by A. O. L. in 1923. The study also proves that every sufficiently large rational number can be expressed as the sum of four values taken by a certain quadratic form, which was previously known for a certain limited case. The method used in this study can potentially be applied to resolve similar problems for both quadratic and cubic forms in various other domains.

The vast amounts of data produced by modern spectral instruments make automatic matching techniques necessary. As these instruments continue to improve, traditional methods are struggling to keep up. We propose a novel approach using astrophotonic concepts to enhance the efficiency of automatic matching. By representing spectra as a combination of key features, we explore the use of compressive sensing and relevant prior information to achieve this goal. A proposed algorithm is successfully applied to a test dataset, and comparative results suggest that this approach significantly reduces processing times while maintaining high accuracy levels.

Medication Pair Discovery, also known as Next Medication Prediction, is a vital task in computational healthcare that involves predicting whether adding a second medication to an existing pair, given a patient's history, leads to a specific outcome. We have compiled a comprehensive dataset called MEDICATE, comprising 2.3 million instances of documented pairs and 550,000 implicit negative instances, to evaluate the effectiveness of advanced deep learning models in this context. Our state-of-the-art results on 3 crucial downstream tasks, utilizing diverse model architectures, cohesive embeddings, and task-specific embeddings, demonstrate the value of the data. Furthermore, the availability of the dataset and initial model outcomes are publicly accessible via the link provided.

Consider a Wentzell-type process constructed from Brownian motion, whose dynamics are governed by a differential equation with discontinuous coefficients. This paper provides an "It\^o-Wentzell formula" for a function applied to the process, where the function may also change over time and space. The proposed construction relies on approximations based on piecewise linear interpolation of the driving Brownian motion, extending previous work on average case complexity for nonlinear differential equations. The main result is an derivation of the It\^o-Wentzell formula under specific conditions, established through a combination of discrete and continuous approaches.

In the realm of Federated Learning, improving models from low-quality data contributors has been a longstanding challenge. To address this issue without increasing their data quality, we've developed an innovative approach called Random Stroll from Uniform Models (FedRU). This new method allows a primary model to learn from a diverse array of data sources by allowing some data contributors to randomly explore their data and make model updates. The concept of random walks is also applied to increase the model's exposure to a wider array of data types, following Chebyshev's inequality. By incorporating the random stroll mechanism, our approach is capable of consistently enhancing the overall performance of the model, as shown in our experiments.

We have developed a numerically efficient method to simulate three-dimensional chaotic flows of inertially sheared turbulence, which allows for an accurate prediction of the energy spectrum's slope at $-3.8$ based on initial and final states in simulations of varying durations. This approach is particularly beneficial due to its reduced computational demands in comparison to traditional methods, while its straightforward framework facilitates its application in supercomputing environments. Furthermore, our technique involves direct estimates of the Lagrangian coherent structures and the fractional powers of the Kolmogorov scale, which in turn provide insights into the characteristics of coherent vortices within the flow and their formation times. These features are visually depicted through volume-rendered images along with 2D slices.

The effects of substance abuse and mental health disorders on incarcerated individuals are well-documented, but the research on the associated behaviors is often fragmented. Studies have also highlighted the limitations of the current criminal justice and incarceration systems in effectively addressing these issues. Given that many offenders lack access to essential psychological services and these systems fail to positively impact mental health, this study aims to model how mental health disorders develop within the criminal justice system and explore the potential benefits of mandatory treatment programs for incarcerated individuals. By utilizing a simple framework for psychological well-being, this study A) implements a basic model for the criminal justice system with various outcomes including successful rehabilitation, employment, further incarceration, and use of public assistance within communities; B) examines how specific mental health disorders affect these systems; and C) investigates the effects of mandatory treatment on this population. This study A) employs a dynamic model of psychological well-being to represent thinking, motivation, and moral reasoning within the system; B) incorporates mental health disorders into this model to explore how they affect behavior and moral reasoning and to explore potential benefits of increased incentives for good behavior and access to essential needs that come from treatment; and C) applies these frameworks to analyze the effects of mandatory treatment on incarceration and recidivism rates and public assistance use within communities. By incorporating empirical data into the model and simulating different policies, this research indicates that the primary obstacles to positive mental well-being exhibited by incarcerated individuals do not necessarily result from inherent flaws in their moral reasoning, but rather from impaired

Mildly supervised semantic segmentation combines elements of self-supervised and supervised learning, utilizing massive unlabeled medical image data to boost model performance.  Mildly supervised methods have shown promise in reducing the need for labor-intensive, time-consuming supervised annotation.  However, a significant limitation exists: current models tend to overfit to the available annotated regions. To address this issue, we introduce a novel, straightforward consistency regularization technique for medDICE, a mildly supervised network.  By applying this proposed technique, we create an improved model called Awkwardly Basic medDICE (Awk medDICE), which delivers state-of-the-art results in several medical image segmentation tasks, including pancreatic and kidney segmentation.  Our research demonstrates that incorporating our proposed strategy significantly enhances model accuracy across multiple evaluation metrics such as Dice Similarity Coefficient, Sensitivity, and Specificity.  Furthermore, we also show substantial improvements in overall model robustness when utilizing massive medDICE pre-trained networks in several medical image segmentation tasks.  Notably, the advancement achieved through our technique also holds when employing diverse loss functions and medDICE loss variants.  We make the source code of Awk medDICE publicly available for other researchers to utilize and build upon.  The project can be found at: https://github.com/zheng3571/Awkwardly_Basic_Constant_regularization_technique_for_Mildly_Supervised_HTC_Image_Segmentation

The ATLAS Jet Calorimeter (LAr+TCAL) constitutes a significant component of the ATLAS detector used in the search for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). With the LHC operating at increased luminosity and energy, existing detection systems are being strained, necessitating faster and more efficient data processing. The ATLAS experiment is preparing for Run 3 by upgrading its hardware, including upgrading its trigger and data acquisition systems. A critical aspect of this upgrade involves developing novel, high-speed interface boards that can interface with the LAr calorimeter's detection modules using the Flexible Flexible Flexible Flexible (FLEX) protocol. As a part of this upgrade process, a new board based on Xilinx UltraScale+ architecture has been designed and constructed, providing an 8-channel interface and enhanced data processing capabilities. With this new board, researchers have demonstrated significant improvements in data transfer rates and processing speeds, making it an ideal platform for running complex algorithms and analyzing data in real-time.

This paper introduces a novel approach to articulated depiction known as ANR,
utilizing Assumptively Complete Representations. ANR encompasses a versatile
method for creating detailed 3D models of complex objects with numerous degrees of
freedom. By employing a parametric object model and implicit completion through
Neural Fields, ANR achieves a balanced depiction that is both comprehensive and
accurate in areas corresponding to the modeled features. We demonstrate ANR's
effectiveness on a 12-degree of freedom human model, and its advantages over
alternative techniques in terms of depiction quality and computational
efficiency. Furthermore, ANR's approach can be applied to other objects with high
numbers of degrees of freedom.

A significant obstacle in understanding how chaos evolves within complex and irregular shapes is lack of clarity about their dynamic behavior. To address this issue, we have developed a novel graph neural network approach that can extract features from an atomistic system and provide an interpretable representation of its dynamics. By utilizing a basic model of a particle confined within a billiard with an irregular boundary, we have shown that this graph neural network framework effectively supersedes traditional methods like dimensionality reduction and time series analysis. Specifically, it enables us to clearly identify transitions between different dynamic behavior patterns and chaos control methods that other approaches struggle to do. In shapley explanation, we can interpret the network's predictive capabilities and the latent variables it processes. Overall, our research presents a robust and transparent method for analyzing complex dynamic systems that goes beyond the limitations of existing dimensionality reduction and time series analysis techniques.

Consider $X_1, \dots, X_n$ as independent random variables, where the expected value of $X_i$ is a function $g(\theta_i)$, with $\theta_i$ being a parameter associated with $X_i$. Suppose we are interested in assessing the average of these parameters, denoted as $\bar{\theta} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \theta_i$, using a generalized maximum likelihood method. This paper extends the approach introduced by Panjer and Panjer to evaluate the average of parameters and compares it to traditional methods, including the classical and generalized minimum variance unbiased assessment. As part of the comparison, a digital dataset is used to analyze the mean squared error for various methods, focusing on scenarios involving independent Poisson and normal variables. Additionally, the paper considers applying these methods to sampling, particularly in the context of obtaining an estimate for the average of parameters in a superpopulation model.

Educational institutions are gradually adopting Adaptive Learning technology to personalize learning and incorporate Knowledge Tracing as a method to assess student performance over time. Knowing how to evaluate and compare different Knowledge Tracing models is crucial for developing effective learning assessment systems, yet the standard benchmarks for comparing traditional and deep learning based tracing models are limited, especially for deep learning approaches. To bridge this gap, we present pyKT, a flexible Python framework that provides a robust platform for testing and comparing Knowledge Tracing models. PyKT includes pre-built models, custom model support, evaluation metrics, and a unified benchmarking system, streamlining the process of developing and evaluating different Learning Tracing models.

Given a smooth, non-compact manifold $M$, a key property of a second-order, uniformly elliptic, $m$-tuple of differential operators $\mathcal{A} = (A_1,\dots,A_m)$ is that its associated differential operator $\Lambda = \sum_{j=1}^m A_j^*$ has a discrete spectrum composed of an increasing sequence of real numbers. This characteristic holds true if and only if each operator $A_j$ has a smooth domain equivalent to that of its compacted version. Furthermore, when this condition is met, for any positive real number $\beta$ less than the dimension of the manifold, there exists a smooth domain where the original operator $\mathcal{A}$ can be compactified, resulting in a discrete spectrum for all associated operators $A_j^*$ with spectrum consisting of an increasing sequence of real numbers.

Proofs generated by solvers for first-order logic typically aim at resolving a contradictory set of assumptions, thereby demonstrating the impossibility of deriving false conclusions. Research in this area has primarily focused on exploiting such proofs for their reductio ad absurdum properties. However, recent advancements suggest utilizing external verification for additional benefits, including software stability enhancement, intellectual property protection, and legal contract enforcement. To facilitate external verification, it is imperative that proofs from various solvers can be standardized into a common format that external verifiers can process seamlessly. This research effort seeks to create a comprehensive open standard set of formats that encompass representations from a range of solvers, covering topics such as Datalog, DPLL, SMT, and first-order logic.

In the context of federated learning, a well-known challenge is that models tend to converge slowly in constrained gradient regions due to limited updates per client device per session. Although researchers have developed various techniques to overcome Constrained Gradient Regions (CGR), they often introduce complexities in implementation, compromised privacy protections, or additional computational costs. In this paper, we investigate and quantify the behavior of unconstrained and constrained gradient regions in a theoretically modeled federated learning context. Our analysis of buffered synchronous aggregation reveals that this popular algorithm can be seen as an implicit method that effectively navigates through CGR by taking smaller steps in constrained regions and larger steps in regions of unconstrained gradients. Our findings suggest that in many practical scenarios involving non-i.i.d. data, the implicit CGR-solving technique of the buffered synchronous aggregation algorithm can lead to comparable accuracy to fully independent linear models. Moreover, our research highlights that the same algorithm experiences only a minimal decrease ($\sqrt3$ factor) in convergence rate when compared to constrained regions traversing methods, making our approach redundant for most practical scenarios.

Lately, automatic speech recognition systems have been increasingly focused on high-resolution systems, as they have shown significant improvements in accurately recognizing difficult-to-distinguish sounds, which can be attributed to advances in neural networks. This trend can be compared to advancements in medical imaging, where increased detail in imaging techniques aids in the detection and analysis of issues. Building on this, researchers explored whether language transfer in ASR would benefit from using detailed models. They trained models to translate sentences from English to Spanish and used the models' predictions as input to high-fidelity English recognizers. Surprisingly, they found that while these models achieve excellent performance in their specific translation tasks, they struggle when it comes to matching them with native languages. However, they also discovered that incorporating a simple model of language distribution can significantly enhance the quality of models that are being transferred.

The Twitch community, comprising over 40 million fans of live streaming, has a well-established online presence that includes bio pages detailing streamer attributes, backgrounds, and details about their shows, episodes, and viewer counts. These profiles also feature personal links representing association with other game studios or esports teams within the graph of interconnected entities. Recently, a data scientist embarked on a project to build models predicting Twitch streamer connections based on their involvement in common game titles, past experiences, and other relevant information. To facilitate this research, they compiled a comprehensive dataset of Twitch streamer nodes, pre-processing the Wikipedia web of knowledge, which now serves as an ideal platform for assessing novel embedding techniques designed to capture the proximal and structural roles within knowledge graphs.

Our study suggests that any evidence for a particle at $f_X \sim 1400$ $\pm 20$ MeV currently lacks sufficient statistical significance.  Additionally, the EULC of the current dataset suggests the absence of significant contribution from $f_X$ at $f_X \sim 1450$ MeV.  Based on existing data, more research is necessary to definitively determine whether the signal at $1500$ MeV represents a unique resonance or is in fact the $\rho^0(1450)$.  To do so, increasing the dataset size to several times the current $B$-meson decays is essential.  With a dataset of $300$ pb$^{-1}$, we estimate that the significance of any deviation from the predicted spectrum due to $\mathcal{A}_T$ will reach a maximum of $2.6\sigma$.  To achieve a significance of $5\sigma$, a dataset of $4.5$ nb$^{-1}$ is required.  With such an increased dataset, we project that the resolution of any such deviation will reach a minimum of $18$ MeV.

Recent astrophysical observations suggest a new phenomenon known as the "Marshland," which refers to disks exhibiting properties between terrestrial habitats and the dark realms of space. These formations arise due to a substance that constitutes a significant portion of the cosmic matter. If this mysterious component is comprised of primordial black holes (PBHs), additional constraints on the dark matter-PBH mass ratio emerge, which in turn affects other limits set by the Planck mission and supernovae observations. Furthermore, a specific mass range of dark matter PBHs remains unexplored by current cosmological data. This unique void exists regardless of the Marshland existence.

A novel algorithm called SE-DFRLP has been developed to enhance the precise force control of series elastic actuators (SEAs). This method integrates a strong transmission force estimator with an indirect compliance control system that considers the dynamics of the SEA's elastic element. A theoretical analysis utilizing a compliance transformation approach proves that, as the control parameters are optimized, closed-loop forces generated by the SEA match the desired forces. A simulation using a high-fidelity SEA model demonstrates that optimal control parameters lead to minimal difference between actual and desired closed-loop forces. Furthermore, compared to conventional indirect compliance control methods, SE-DFRLP exhibits superior performance in achieving precise force control of SEAs.

Liquid crystals in simple, two-dimensional systems with one-dimensional particles exhibit a nuanced relationship between their structural order and dynamic properties, particularly when the particles interact through short-range forces, resulting in 'smectic' phases that can be further classified as 'solid-like' or 'fluid-like'. Through an innovative combination of experimental techniques and computational analyses, this study provides direct, detailed insights into the microstructural differences between these two smectic variants, revealing distinct fracture behaviors that manifest as elastic bending of fractured segments. Moreover, the fluid-like smectic phase is found to possess a tensile strength capable of surpassing its shear modulus by an order of magnitude.

We investigated a 3D SU(Nc) lattice gauge theory with a set of scalar fields interacting through a variety of terms, with the scalar fields transforming under the fundamental representation of SU(Nc). Lattice phase diagrams were analyzed for two specific instanton-like terms, with the expectation that they drive the transition from confined to Coulombic phase, or facilitate a transition to Higgs phase. An investigation into an effective potential function yielded insight into the nature of the transition, which was found to be first order in certain instances, while in others it was second order and associated with an emergent U(1) symmetry. For an instanton-like term characterized by a deformation of the potential, phase transitions were found to occur when the confining string was broken, with the critical exponent matching that of the 3D O(2) model, indicating a Higgs phase characterized by an emergent symmetry. Numerical simulations were also conducted to verify whether the transition when the deformation was applied to the kinetic term was continuous, which was found not to be the case, as Coulombic and confined phases coexisted at the transition point.

Achieving fully autonomous navigation for underwater robots without human supervision or pre-defined maps proves to be a challenging task. A significant breakthrough was made possible by the development of Value Function-based Navigation, which successfully combined goal-directed movement with map-based localization features. However, existing approaches struggle to effectively handle dynamic environments due to their reliance on robotic trials for data collection and use of high-dimensional states that slow down the learning process. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel approach using a sparse Gaussian process to create an environment model capable of accurately modeling and predicting the movement of objects in three-dimensional space. By leveraging this model, our method can efficiently navigate around obstacles in real-time while in pursuit of targets. We have successfully tested our approach on real-world missions with an underwater vehicle in a complex, dynamically changing environment, where we observed unexpected movements of a large object, and were able to complete the mission without prior knowledge of the target location or object movement patterns.

This paper explores the concept of uniform-depth sorting networks, specifically those with comparable element comparison spans. It builds upon previous research, advancing the record for 64 elements while establishing new benchmarks for smaller sizes ranging from 10 to 32 elements. The study also introduces a method for creating sorting networks with consistent depths based on existing networks, ultimately leading to a 64-element sorting network with a depth of 28 comparisons.

In General Relativity, non-uniform two-fluid stars are explored using realistic models of stellar matter, with assumptions made about each fluid's density, motion, and interfluid forces being reasonable. Similarities between these GR models and their special relativistic counterparts are highlighted, particularly in terms of both fluids potentially rotating with the same angular velocity and contributing to the overall stability of the celestial body, an aspect with potential significance in the context of neutron stars composed of multiple phases or materials, where the more massive fluid often contributes more to the total mass but not always more to the radius.

The origin of spiral arms in galaxy disks remains a mystery in modern astronomy. 
Although several theories exist, the lack of sufficient detail in existing simulations prevents a comprehensive comparison with real observations. 
To overcome this limitation, we utilized high-resolved, realistic simulations that accurately depict the dynamics of a typical galaxy like the Milky Way, featuring a bulge, disk, and multiple stellar populations in this study. 
By analyzing the order-disorder parameter, commonly associated with the formation of spiral patterns in living systems, we were able to demonstrate that the arms seen in these simulations share certain characteristics with analogues found in self-organizing systems. 
The results also revealed that the arms' shape and tightness are influenced by the distribution of dark matter in the galaxy, as well as by rapid rotational curves. 
This discovery suggests a potential mechanism that could contribute to the self-organizing formation of spiral patterns in galaxy disks.

GALACTICSIMs, state-of-the-art collision simulations that incorporate advanced physical principles, enable a deeper understanding of how galaxy mergers evolve. These simulations utilize high-resolution 3-bit rate limited magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) simulations, enabling researchers to analyze the impact of magnetic fields on galaxy collisions. This study undertakes an extensive usage test of these simulations by studying the merger of two massive spiral galaxies with similar masses. Over a period of 0.7 billion years, the simulations track the interaction as they slowly approach each other, ultimately experiencing a head-on collision and experiencing a significant impact on their stellar disks. During the collision, weak magnetic fields do not impede the development of density waves or delay shock waves in the galaxies' disks. However, higher strength magnetic fields restrict gas collimation, expand the elliptical regions of dense matter, and inhibit the concentration of massive clusters. As a result, higher strength magnetic fields also affect the distribution of massive stars and star formation patterns. Furthermore, magnetic fields alter the orbital paths of massive clusters and, in stronger field scenarios, these clusters become entangled, exchanging orbital positions. This study paves the way for a deeper understanding of how magnetic fields influence galaxy collisions and the formation of massive star clusters, ultimately contributing to our knowledge of the galaxy's stellar population and magnetic field dynamics.

The primary issue we face is the limited size and severe imbalance of medical datasets used to train deep neural networks to predict the severity of COVID-19 symptoms from chest CT scans, with available data consisting of only a few hundred labeled scans and hundreds of negative labels. To address this problem effectively, we introduce a novel approach called Infection-aware Contrastive Mixup Classification, which incorporates a contrastive loss to enhance the accuracy of symptom prediction. By comparing the similarity between chest CT scans labeled as positive, negative, and unlabeled, our method enables the model to learn to differentiate between healthy lungs and lungs affected by COVID-19, thereby improving the performance of symptom prediction on unlabeled data. Experimental evaluations on the publicly available COVID-ATLAS dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques, achieving a weighted F1-score of 0.87, a substantial improvement over the previous best score of 0.73. Furthermore, our research reveals that our model outperforms existing methods on unlabeled data and excels in visualizing lung severity maps, showcasing the effectiveness of our innovative solution.

Most current systems for correcting grammatical errors rely heavily on large amounts of annotated data within a specific domain. The necessity for extensive data labeling and the rapid obsolescence of popular domains due to frequent language changes are significant limitations of these systems. To address these issues, we developed a novel meta-learning approach for GER that allows a model to effectively adapt to new domains with very little (few-shot) data. The random forest model, enhanced by this multi-task meta-learning framework, can efficiently perform few-shot domain transfers after being initially trained on multiple source domains. The effectiveness of our system in achieving accurate few-shot domain transfer was demonstrated through thorough experiments, particularly in correcting Chinese GEDT sentences, compared against baseline models.

Corporations, governmental bodies, and non-profit organizations frequently release financial statistics that have been rounded to the nearest whole number. Researchers, consumers, and policy-makers often depend on these published numbers to understand the overall situation. However, since rounded figures can represent a range of possible values, the actual value of each reported number is not precisely known. This uncertainty arises because each rounded integer has its own specific range, which may or may not include the calculated average of those ranges. In situations where the average falls outside of these ranges, the exact average cannot be determined. To address this limitation, a statistical model has been developed to provide revised estimates for totals based on available information about individual rounded values. The effectiveness of this approach was demonstrated through detailed financial data from a corporate company over the course of 18 years.

In our studies, we synthesized and investigated the optical and magnetic properties of the cubic centered honeycomb gapped material GdInO$_3$. Using the Rutherford fore-edge method, we created polycrystalline samples of GdInO$_3$, which were then analyzed for their optical and magnetic behavior. Transmittance spectra showed two distinct interband transitions at 3.4 eV and 4.2 eV, with the former exceeding the latter in intensity. Further examinations through far-infrared spectra and Neel temperature measurements indicated that GdInO$_3$ exhibits localized and collective excitations, as well as antiferromagnetic properties, with the Neel temperature being 12 K. These studies also revealed that the exchange interactions between magnetic ions were both bi-directional and nonexchange in nature.

We are examining the connection between the genuine and the simulated in a setting where the goal is to divide a set of non-divisible resources among non-cooperative participants. Our analysis reveals an interesting correlation: as the number of resources being divided increases, the differences between the simulated and actual efficiency of a situation become less pronounced. Based on this finding, we utilize this correlation to estimate bounds for estimating the existence of a state in which simulated efficiency is maintained even when participants falsely declare their preferences for the resources.

The prevalent view on determining an ideal mapping from a source domain to a target domain relies on minimizing distribution discrepancies between the two domains' transformed feature spaces. In our research, we question the necessity of this criterion and propose that the source and target domains do not need to map onto each other. As a result, we develop a novel, indirect transformation technique that employs two independent neural networks. One of these maps the source domain to a third domain, while the other does the same for the target domain. This innovative approach paves the way for a new, indirect optimization objective. Surprisingly, this objective can be interpreted as finding the two most efficient domain adaptation neural networks. By employing simple regularization techniques, we can effectively combine this objective with the source and target domain feature optimization problems. The proposed method yields remarkable, state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets. Moreover, we observe that our indirect approach consistently outperforms its direct counterpart, especially in cases involving significant domain shifts and high-dimensional data.

We have discovered an ultra-stable disk (USD) surrounding galaxy UGC 8839, 
characterized by an inner region that maintains a constant rotation velocity 
independent of distance from the galaxy center. This USD typically comprises the 
inner sections of galaxy disks. Researchers define two essential criteria for 
identifying these structures. 
UGC 8839 exhibits both characteristics with a region spanning 1.6 to 8.4 kiloparsecs 
where the rotational velocities remain consistent at approximately 100 kilometers 
per second. 
Analyzing the dynamical mass distribution within this galaxy reveals a mass 
density proportional to $r^{-4}$ within the USD, which however does not necessarily 
apply to other USDs. 
Furthermore, examining the stellar mass density within this region shows a mass 
density proportional to $r^{-4.5}$ based on fitting the SPITRE far-infrared data 
to the radiative transfer model. 
Utilizing the gravitational potential derived from this mass distribution, we 
calculated the stellar orbital stability and found that most stellar orbits within 
this region are stable. 
UGC 8839's USD exhibits a dynamic mass distribution distinct from gas-rich 
galaxies but shares similarities with dynamically dominant galaxies in terms of 
their stellar orbit stability. 
Additionally, we observed that the dynamic and photometric mass densities within 
this galaxy's USD diverge, a phenomenon also present in other dynamo galaxies.
